Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) provides superior spatial resolution, reduced blooming, and multi-energy spectral data, yet its ultra-high-resolution (UHR) datasets frequently suffer from increased noise and complex spectral information that require advanced processing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to fully exploit PCD-CT's advantages. This narrative review aims to synthesize the current evidence on AI applications in PCD-CT for CAD imaging, evaluate their technical performance and clinical potential, identify limitations, and propose future directions. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. Original English-language studies applying AI techniques to PCD-CT data for CAD imaging were included, and categorized using a 5-level translational framework. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Thirty single-center studies were identified and grouped into three main categories. In image quality improvement, denoising models achieved 60-96% noise reduction while preserving spatial and spectral fidelity. Radiomics studies (the largest group) identified specific texture features in myocardium, plaques, pericoronary, and epicardial adipose tissue associated with coronary artery calcium severity, hypercholesterolemia, aging, and CAD presence, although feature reproducibility was only moderate. Automated detection/quantification/segmentation tools demonstrated high reproducibility, improved stenosis quantification, substantial workflow benefits, and promising CT-fractional flow reserve (FFR) performance with strong intra-individual agreement to EID-CT. CONCLUSIONS: AI has shown promising technical advancements when applied to PCD-CT for CAD imaging. However, the evidence base remains limited by small sample sizes, single-center and single-scanner designs, lack of external validation, and absence of outcome-driven studies. Future research should focus on multicenter prospective validation, standardized protocols, human-in-the-loop systems, and clinical impact assessment to support the safe and effective translation of AI-enhanced PCD-CT into routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based quantitative assessment of fatty infiltration in skeletal muscle and myocardium: a narrative review of technical principles, differences in clinical applications, and future directions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Fatty infiltration of skeletal muscle and myocardium is associated with muscle dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, and arrhythmias. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based fat quantification techniques are being increasingly applied in the skeletal muscle and myocardium, but no review has systematically compared measurements in these areas. The purpose of this review was to compare the quantification of skeletal muscle and myocardial fat in terms of technical principles, clinical applications, and research paradigms. METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, relevant journal databases, and conference proceedings (e.g., Proceedings of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine) were searched up to December 2025 for English-language literature with the following keywords: "MRI", "fat quantification", "Dixon", "magnetic resonance spectroscopy", "T1 mapping", "T2 mapping", "skeletal muscle", "myocardium", "epicardial adipose tissue", and "artificial intelligence". Original research, reviews, and consensus statements were included. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Literature onthe Dixon method, magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), mapping techniques, magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF), and artificial intelligence (AI) was summarized. In skeletal muscle, the Dixon method is the practical standard, demonstrating robust multicenter reproducibility and established functional correlations in muscular dystrophy, sarcopenia, and inflammatory myopathies. In the myocardium, fat quantification relies mainly on mapping techniques, especially T1 mapping and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) quantification, as Dixon and MRS techniques are limited by cardiac motion, thin walls, and low-fat content. Myocardial mapping detects subclinical injury, and increased EAT volume is independently associated with myocardial fibrosis. These techniques aid diagnosis and risk stratification in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, diabetic cardiomyopathy, and Fabry disease. AI is driving automated segmentation and prognostic prediction in both fields. CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle fat quantification is predominantly conducted with the Dixon method and is relatively mature, whereas myocardial fat quantification relies mainly on mapping techniques and lacks standardization. The multicenter validation of approaches related to skeletal muscle and related experiences in automated segmentation and AI application can inform practices in the quantification of myocardial fat. Combined cardiac-skeletal muscle assessment and integrated multiparametric imaging are promising future directions in the broader field.

articles.title: Predicting acute radiation dermatitis in breast cancer patients using artificial intelligence: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute radiation dermatitis (ARD) is a common toxicity of breast cancer radiotherapy that affects quality of life. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have been increasingly developed to predict ARD, but their methodological quality and clinical readiness remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate AI-based prediction models for ARD. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase (Ovid), Web of Science, and MEDLINE (Ovid) was conducted for studies published up to December 1, 2025. Studies were eligible if they developed and/or validated AI-based models for predicting ARD in patients with breast cancer receiving radiotherapy. Data were extracted using the CHARMS framework. Model quality, applicability, and risk of bias were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool plus Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST + AI) tool. Given the substantial heterogeneity among studies, a qualitative synthesis was performed. RESULTS: Nineteen studies involving 8,506 patients were included, with sample sizes ranging from 20 to 2,058. Most studies were single-center (16/19), and only three were multicenter. Validation area under the curve (AUC) values ranged from 0.66 to 0.99. The models incorporated clinical, dosimetric, radiomics, and/or dosiomics features, with 5-154 predictors in the final models. Calibration and decision curve analysis were rarely reported, and no study performed external validation. Most studies had a high or unclear risk of bias according to PROBAST + AI, mainly related to small sample sizes, incomplete reporting, and lack of external validation. CONCLUSIONS: Although current AI-based models for predicting ARD in breast cancer radiotherapy demonstrate promising discriminatory performance, their methodological limitations and lack of external validation limit their readiness for routine clinical implementation. Future studies with more rigorous designs, standardized outcome assessment, transparent reporting, and independent external validation are required to facilitate clinical translation.

articles.title: HSMD: A Hilbert-scanning mamba dense network for 3D MRI reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Long MRI acquisition times motivate the use of k-space undersampling for accelerated imaging, but undersampling often introduces aliasing artifacts and structural detail loss. Existing 2D slice-wise reconstruction methods fail to fully exploit inter-slice anatomical correlations. This study develops a Hilbert-Scanning Mamba Dense Network (HSMD) for high-quality 3D MRI reconstruction, which leverages inter-slice contextual information to improve reconstruction fidelity. The proposed HSMD consists of a Shallow Feature Extraction Module (SFEM) and five cascaded Multi-Directional Spatial Attention (MDSA) modules. The SFEM is responsible for extracting local detailed features and coarse-scale structural context from undersampled MRI inputs. The MDSA modules extract and fuse multi-directional spatial information along the depth, height, and width dimensions to enhance the representation of 3D structural features. Furthermore, a multi-directional Hilbert selective state-space scanning strategy is introduced into MDSA to capture long-range spatial dependencies within 3D volumetric data, thereby improving structural representation while preserving spatial locality. Experimental results on the BraTS and UCSF-PDGM datasets under diverse acceleration factors validate that the proposed HSMD achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The HSMD exhibits excellent capability in 3D undersampled MRI reconstruction, holding promising prospects for efficient and reliable clinical MRI applications.

articles.title: Integrated deep learning reconstruction combining phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate integrated deep learning reconstruction (Integrated DLR), which combines phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution, for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) by comparing it with compressed sensing (CS) and deep learning-based denoising reconstruction (Denoising DLR). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective study included 47 patients scanned on a single-vendor 3-T system. Three DWI datasets were reconstructed from identical raw data using CS, Denoising DLR, and Integrated DLR. Two radiologists rated overall image quality, noise, artifact, and prostate delineation. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was assessed in all patients. In 21 patients with pathologically confirmed prostate cancer, we assessed lesion conspicuity, lesion localization/anatomical relationship, Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version 2.1 DWI scores, apparent lesion contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Comparisons were performed using Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Scores for overall image quality, noise, and prostate delineation were highest with Integrated DLR, followed by Denoising DLR and CS, for both readers (all p < 0.001); apparent SNR showed the same pattern (p < 0.001). Artifact scores did not differ among methods. Lesion conspicuity differed among methods for Reader 2 (p = 0.044) but not for Reader 1 (p = 0.199), whereas Integrated DLR yielded the highest lesion localization/anatomical relationship scores for both readers (both p < 0.001). Integrated DLR also yielded the highest apparent CNR and lesion ADC (both p < 0.001), while PI-RADS DWI scores were unchanged. CONCLUSION: Integrated DLR improved prostate DWI image quality and lesion visibility compared with CS and Denoising DLR, potentially facilitating visual assessment of prostate DWI.

articles.title: Deep learning-derived functional MRI connectivity maps of cervical spinal cord segments during hand grasping.
articles.abstract: Task-based fMRI of the cervical spinal cord is limited by physiological noise and small sample sizes. The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based denoising framework can improve the detection of task-dependent functional connectivity between cervical spinal segments using generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analysis. An open dataset of 26 healthy adults performing a hand-grasp task with alternating right- and left-hand blocks during 3 T fMRI was analyzed. A CNN with Inception V3 transfer learning (91.0% slice-level and 89.2% block-level accuracy) was trained to classify grasp versus rest, and the trained model was then utilized to derive denoised time series from masks of the spinal segments C5-C8. A gPPI model with a C6 ventral horn seed was evaluated using FDR correction and permutation testing (n = 1000). C6 showed positive task-dependent connectivity with C7 (β = 0.72, p = 0.003) and C8 (β = 0.58, p = 0.018), and negative connectivity with C5 (β = -0.31, p = 0.041), which is broadly consistent with the organization of the cervical myotomes. The C6-C5 effect was marginal and was not detected when conventional time series were used (p = 0.21), and therefore it requires replication. Grad-CAM maps aligned with ventral horn motor pools (Dice = 0.89 at C7). These results suggest that deep learning-based denoising may increase the sensitivity of spinal cord fMRI to segmental connectivity, although validation in larger cohorts is needed.

articles.title: Sex-based variability of water-equivalent diameter (Dw) and dosimetric parameters in adult head computed tomography (CT): implications for protocol optimisation.
articles.abstract: AIM: The water-equivalent diameter (Dw) is increasingly used to express patient size in computed tomography (CT). Sex-related differences in Dw are documented in the chest and abdomen, but data for adult head CT remain scarce. The aims of this study were to compare Dw and dosimetric parameters (tube current-time product [mAs], volume computed tomography dose index [CTDIvol], size-specific dose estimates based on water-equivalent diameter [SSDEw], dose-length product [DLP], effective dose [EDw]) between men and women undergoing adult noncontrast head CT and to assess the relationship of Dw with mAs and SSDEw. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 109 adult noncontrast head CT examinations (67 men and 42 women) performed with a standardised protocol on a 16-slice CT. Dw and dose indices were calculated using automated segmentation and compared between sexes (independent t-test); relationships were assessed by linear regression. RESULTS: No significant differences were found between sexes for Dw, mAs, CTDIvol, or SSDEw (all P > 0.05). DLP and EDw were slightly higher in men (P = 0.0337 and P = 0.0445), mainly owing to larger Dw and scan lengths. Dw correlated positively with mAs (women r = 0.57; men r = 0.46; P < 0.001) and SSDEw (women r = 0.52; men r = 0.38; P ≤ 0.002). CONCLUSION: In this single-centre series, limited intersex variability in adult head CT dose metrics supports standardised protocols irrespective of sex. Dw is most valuable for dose audit, quality control, and identification of outlying examinations; its contribution to optimisation, which also requires image quality assessment, should be confirmed in prospective multicentre studies.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound-based imaging modalities for assessing residual axillary lymph node disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate identification of residual axillary lymph node (ALN) disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is essential for treatment planning and for evaluating potential surgical de-escalation. We assessed the diagnostic performance of conventional ultrasonography (US), shear-wave elastography (SWE), artificial intelligence (AI)/radiomics, and multimodal ultrasound-based models for post-NAC axillary restaging. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through December 2025. Histopathology after axillary surgery was the reference standard, and residual axillary nodal disease (ypN+) was uniformly defined as the positive target condition. Study-level 2×2 tables were harmonized to this direction. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Bivariate random-effects models and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves were used for modality groups with a sufficient number of independent studies; the positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) were pooled with random-effects models. Potentially overlapping cohorts were examined in sensitivity analyses. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; registration No. CRD420251271199). RESULTS: A total of 14 articles were included in the systematic review, 10 of which contributed 12 test-level datasets to the quantitative synthesis. For conventional US (six studies), the pooled sensitivity was 0.55 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.36-0.73], the pooled specificity was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84), the area under the HSROC curve (AUC) was 0.78, and the pooled PLR and NLR were 2.47 (95% CI: 1.42-4.28) and 0.54 (95% CI: 0.30-0.95), respectively. AI/radiomics models (three studies) showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.80-0.98), a specificity of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.60-0.94), and an AUC of 0.94; however, likelihood-ratio CIs were wide, and the bivariate covariance estimate reached the boundary. Evidence for SWE was limited to two potentially overlapping reports, and only one multimodal combined-model study had a complete harmonized 2×2 table. At a 40% pretest probability, a negative conventional US result reduced the posttest probability of residual nodal disease to approximately 26%. CONCLUSIONS: Conventional US alone does not reliably exclude residual axillary nodal disease after NAC. AI/radiomics approaches show promising diagnostic performance, but the evidence for this is sparse, heterogeneous, and imprecise. The currently available data do not support definitive modality ranking or omission of axillary surgery on the basis of imaging alone, and prospective multicenter external validation is required.

articles.title: Quantification of fat content in the prediction of lymph node metastasis in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a study based on dixon-MRI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metastatic tumor infiltration disrupts the normal lymph node (LN) architecture and may result in the loss of the fatty hilum, potentially reducing nodal fat content. The volumetric quantification of nodal fat content using Dixon-magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate Dixon-MRI-derived quantitative nodal fat content in patients with HNSCC and to assess its association with conventional morphological MRI features to develop an integrated predictive model for identifying metastatic LNs. METHODS: This retrospective study included 101 HNSCC patients with 266 metastatic LNs, as well as 52 age- and sex-matched healthy controls with 172 normal LNs, examined between January 2019 and April 2024. All subjects underwent pretreatment Dixon-MRI examination, and quantitative nodal fat parameters, including volumetric fat signal intensity (vFat SI) and volumetric fat fraction (vFF), as well as conventional morphological MRI features, were quantitatively extracted and analyzed. Comparisons between groups were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or Kruskal-Wallis test. Logistic regression was used to develop predictive models for metastatic LNs, and model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the curve (AUC). A P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The HNSCC patient group (median age: 63 years, range: 34-84 years) and control group (median age: 63 years, range: 48-80 years) were analyzed. No significant differences in age and sex were observed between the HNSCC group and the control group (all P>0.05). Metastatic LNs exhibited significantly lower vFat SI (27.50 vs. 51.05, P<0.001) and vFF (6.15 vs. 9.22, P<0.001) compared with normal LNs. Logistic regression analyses indicated that vFF was an independent predictor of metastatic LNs [odds ratio (OR) =0.88, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.78-0.99, P<0.043]. Among the predictive models, the one combining all morphological parameters with vFF achieved the highest AUC (0.910), the sensitivity and specificity were 84.2% and 80.8%, respectively, outperforming the other model (P<0.01 DeLong). CONCLUSIONS: The quantitative parameters derived from Dixon-MRI have certain value in differentiating the status of cervical LNs in HNSCC, suggesting their potential as an adjunctive imaging biomarker for nodal status assessment.

articles.title: Correlation between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and left ventricular myocardial strain in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a cardiac magnetic resonance feature-tracking study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) myocardial strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature tracking enables sensitive detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, factors associated with early post-infarction LV myocardial function following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain incompletely understood, particularly in the context of inflammation-related myocardial injury. The platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) which combines two routinely measured blood cell counts and may reflect the dynamic interplay between platelet recovery and inflammatory dynamics, has emerged as a potential biomarker of systemic inflammatory status. This study investigated the association between PWR and LV myocardial strain in patients with STEMI after PCI. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 222 patients with STEMI who underwent CMR imaging within 1 week after PCI. Demographic information, laboratory test results, and CMR parameters were collected. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup, sensitivity and nonlinear analyses were performed to investigate the association between post-PCI PWR and CMR-derived LV myocardial strain. RESULTS: Patients in the highest PWR quartile had significantly higher LV ejection fraction (LVEF) (53.4% vs. 45.0%, P<0.001) and a smaller median infarct size (IS) (11.9% vs. 18.8%, P=0.006) than those in the lowest quartile (Q1). In the fully adjusted logistic model, higher PWR was independently associated with lower odds of impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS) [odds ratio (OR) 0.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.05-0.30, P<0.001] and impaired global circumferential strain (GCS) (OR 0.18; 95% CI: 0.06-0.49; P=0.001), and with higher odds of preserved global radial strain (GRS) (OR 5.57; 95% CI: 2.06-15.06; P=0.001). RCS analysis showed a linear association between PWR and the odds of LV myocardial strain impairment. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses yielded similar associations. CONCLUSIONS: A higher post-PCI PWR was independently associated with more favorable LV myocardial strain after PCI in patients with STEMI. As a routinely available ratio, PWR may complement the early description of myocardial strain impairment.

articles.title: Investigating the correlation between temporalis, masseter and cervical muscle mass on a single cross-sectional image.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low skeletal muscle mass (SMM) is an established prognostic factor in oncology and is conventionally quantified at the third lumbar vertebra. In brain tumour patients, abdominal imaging is seldom available, and craniofacial measurements from routine brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), temporalis muscle thickness (TMT) and masseter cross-sectional area (MCSA), have been proposed as alternatives. Whether these measurements can substitute for one another, or for cervical [skeletal muscle area at the third vertebra (C3SMA)] and lumbar muscle mass, is unknown. We investigated the correlation and classification agreement between these measurements. METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 247 patients who underwent awake craniotomy at Amsterdam University Medical Center between 2003 and 2020. TMT, MCSA and C3SMA were measured on pre-operative three-dimensional (3D) T1-weighted MRI, and L3 skeletal muscle area (L3SMA) and index (L3SMI) were estimated from C3SMA using a previously established method. TMT was available in 247 patients, MCSA in 239 and C3SMA in 136. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation coefficients, crude and adjusted for body mass index (BMI) and, separately, for age and sex. Low SMM was classified using established cut-off values for TMT (≤6.3 mm in men, ≤5.2 mm in women) and L3SMI (<43.2 cm2/m2) and, as no validated masseter threshold exists, the sex-specific lowest quartile for MCSA. Agreement between classifications was assessed using Cohen kappa and interobserver reliability using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). RESULTS: All pairwise correlations were low: TMT and MCSA r=0.39 (P<0.05, n=239), MCSA and C3SMA r=0.30 (P<0.05, n=136), TMT and estimated L3SMA r=0.24 (P<0.05, n=136) and TMT and C3SMA r=0.20 (P<0.05, n=136). Adjustment for BMI altered the coefficients minimally (TMT and MCSA r=0.37, P<0.001), whereas adjustment for age and sex rendered the association between MCSA and C3SMA non-significant (r=0.11, P=0.20). Among the 136 patients with all three measurements, agreement in classifying low SMM was poor using the thresholds applied (Cohen kappa 0.11 for TMT versus MCSA, 0.07 for MCSA versus L3SMI and 0.01 for TMT versus L3SMI), and only 2 patients (1.5%) were concurrently classified as having low SMM by all three measurements. Interobserver reliability was excellent [ICC 0.919, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.790-0.969 for TMT; ICC 0.987, 95% CI: 0.967-0.995 for MCSA]. CONCLUSIONS: Craniofacial, cervical and estimated lumbar muscle measurements showed low correlations with one another and poor agreement in classifying low SMM using the thresholds applied in this study. As L3SMI was estimated rather than directly measured, non-interchangeability cannot be definitively established, but these findings provide little support for using craniofacial measurements as substitutes for one another or for cervical and lumbar muscle mass.

articles.title: Evaluation of virtual monochromatic imaging combined with metal artifact reduction in low-dose dual-energy computed tomography: a phantom study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metal implants can cause substantial artifacts on computed tomography (CT), and the optimal virtual monochromatic (VM) energy for metal artifact reduction (MAR) remains uncertain. This study assessed metal-artifact reduction and overall image quality on low-dose dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) VM images reconstructed with Smart MAR. METHODS: A multi-energy CT phantom (GPH-75B; Kyoto Kagaku Co., Ltd., Kyoto, Japan) was scanned in DECT mode with a 12-mm titanium rod positioned at the center, right, and superior portions. VM images from 40 to 140 keV were reconstructed with MAR and without MAR (no-MAR). Image quality was assessed according to artifact and structure visibility scores, CT values, standard deviations (SDs), titanium-rod dimensions, structural similarity index (SSIM), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and root mean square error (RMSE). MAR and no-MAR measurements were compared via two-sided paired t-tests. RESULTS: Across the three titanium-rod positions, MAR generally reduced artifacts, improved titanium-rod edge visibility, and reduced geometric distortion compared with no-MAR. At every rod position and energy level, MAR yielded higher SSIM and PSNR and lower RMSE compared to no-MAR (all P values <0.05). At the central position, the transverse-to-longitudinal diameter ratio was 0.94-1.03 with MAR and 0.21-0.81 with no-MAR (all P values <0.001), remaining close to 1.0 at energies ≥60 keV with MAR. For MAR images, adjacent-structure clarity was highest at 60 keV. In both groups, SSIM and PSNR increased with increasing energy, whereas RMSE and image noise decreased. CONCLUSIONS: MAR consistently improved image quality across titanium-rod positions. In terms of artifact reduction, implant depiction, and adjacent-structure visibility, 60 to 80-keV VM images with MAR provided the most favorable overall performance under the tested low-dose conditions.

articles.title: Association of intracranial plaque characteristics and cerebral small vessel disease burden with acute ischemic stroke in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Both intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) and cerebral small-vessel disease (CSVD) contribute to ischemic stroke and have shared underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Thus, the aim of this study was to investigate the value of intracranial plaque and CSVD imaging characteristics in diagnosing ischemic stroke and to clarify the impact of coexisting large and small intracranial vessel disease on stroke risk. METHODS: Patients with ICAD who underwent contrast-enhanced higher-resolution vessel wall magnetic resonance imaging (HRVW-MRI) from January 2021 to April 2024 were enrolled. Plaque features such as intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH), enhancement grade, maximum wall thickness (Max WT), and lumen area (LA) were assessed via HRVW-MRI. A CSVD score was determined through four CSVD imaging markers, including lacunes, white-matter lesions (WMLs), cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVSs), with the possible score ranging from 0 to 4. Binary logistic regression analysis was used to ascertain the associations between imaging characteristics and stroke events. The diagnostic performance of imaging indicators was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. RESULTS: Of the 237 patients (median age 63 years; 154 males) enrolled in the study, 174 experienced stroke. Binary logistic regression revealed that patients with greater Max WT, larger LA, a higher number of CMBs and EPVSs, higher enhancement grade, and higher total CSVD score were more likely to experience stroke (all P values <0.05). Enhancement grade remained a robust independent predictor of stroke across all the examined imaging characteristics (odds ratio =6.56-8.96; P<0.001). The two diagnostic models derived from the combination of plaque and CSVD imaging features yielded a higher area under the curve (0.839; 95% CI: 0.783-0.895; P<0.001; 0.787; 95% CI: 0.722-0.851; P<0.001) than did that of the plaque features alone (0.774; 95% CI: 0.709-0.839; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: The combination of plaque features with CSVD imaging markers provides incremental value for diagnosing stroke occurrence and may aid in the clinical management of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Quantification of in vivo short-echo proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy of the human brain on a clinical whole-body 5-T platform under two different macromolecule modeling approaches.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Short-echo proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) offers valuable insights into endogenous brain metabolites, commonly referred to as the neurochemical profile, enabling identification of critical biomarkers for neurological health and disease. However, the reliable extraction of these quantitative neurochemical profiles at high magnetic fields is significantly challenged by the presence of the underlying macromolecular (MM) background signal. As field strength increases to 5 T, the MM components appear with greater resolution and complexity. Although the effects of MM signals on neurochemical profiling at 3 and 7 T are well documented, their corresponding performance related to neurochemical profiling at 5 T remains uncharacterized. Compared to 3- and 7-T platforms, 5-T platforms theoretically offer a unique balance between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and field homogeneity. This study aimed to evaluate the quality of 5-T short-echo proton magnetic resonance (1H MR) spectra and to compare the effects between incorporating in vivo MMs and simulated MMs on neurochemical profiling. METHODS: Short-echo 1H MR spectra [echo time (TE) =10 ms] were acquired on healthy volunteers at 5-T with a standard stimulated echo acquisition mode (STEAM) sequence. An in vivo MM baseline was first measured via an optimized inversion recovery STEAM (IR-STEAM) sequence [inversion time (TI) =750 ms] and postprocessed to remove residual metabolite signals. Spectral fitting was performed with a linear combination model (LCModel) under two strategies: (I) the experimentally derived in vivo MM baseline and (II) default simulated Voigt functions. Quantification reliability was assessed according to Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) and intermethod concentration differences. RESULTS: The 5-T platform yielded high-quality MM spectra for the in vivo MM baseline, along with spectra with a mean SNR of ~110 and a metabolic linewidth of ~6 Hz for the quantification of the neurochemical profile. Both MM approaches successfully resolved 16 metabolites. Although the default simulated MM functions in the LCModel provided acceptable approximations for high-abundance metabolites [e.g., glutamate (Glu), N-acetylaspartate (NAA), and total creatine (tCr)]-12 neurochemicals with a mean ≤20%-they failed to replicate subtle spectral features at 2.5, 3.2, and 3.5-3.9 ppm. The in vivo MM approach significantly improved the quantification of low-concentration metabolites [e.g., glutamine (Gln), taurine (Tau), ascorbate (Asc), and scyllo-inositol (Scyllo)] and enhanced fitting residual performance. Through use of the in vivo MM baseline, 14 neurochemicals were reliably quantified, with a mean CRLB ≤20%. CONCLUSIONS: This study validated the 5-T platform as a high-performance environment for neurochemical profiling, offering an optimal intermediate between 3 and 7 T. Although simulated MM models are sufficient for major metabolites, a refined in vivo MM baseline is necessary for comprehensive and accurate quantification of the neurochemical profile. This framework provides a robust methodological foundation for future clinical research into metabolic alterations in brain disorders at 5 T.

articles.title: Synthetic MRI and IDEAL-IQ for evaluating microstructural changes in Kager's fat pad and Achilles tendon in amateur marathon runners: a preliminary study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Achilles tendinopathy is common in runners. Kager's fat pad (KFP) biomechanically and metabolically supports Achilles tendon (AT) health. Reliable quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques to noninvasively detect subclinical KFP-AT alterations could provide valuable insights into subclinical tissue adaptations and load responses. The objective of this study was to assess synthetic MRI (SyMRI) and iterative decomposition of water and fat with echo asymmetry and least-squares estimation quantitation (IDEAL-IQ) for monitoring longitudinal microstructural changes in the KFP and AT of amateur marathoners before and after a race. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 17 amateur marathoners and 17 demographically matched healthy controls. The marathoners underwent bilateral ankle MRI at three time points (prerun, 48-hour postrun, and 2-month postrun). The controls received a single baseline scan. SyMRI and IDEAL-IQ sequences generated T1, T2, proton density (PD), proton density fat fraction (PDFF), and R2* maps. On the sagittal slice displaying the maximum cross-section of the AT, KFP was delineated, and the AT was divided into insertion (INS), middle (MID), and muscle-tendon junction (MTJ) segments. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) evaluated cross-sectional group differences and longitudinal changes. Pearson and Spearman analyses assessed correlations between acute KFP and AT quantitative parameter variations (Δ = 48 hours postrun - prerun). RESULTS: Compared to controls, marathoners exhibited a lower PDFF and higher T1 and R2* in KFP (allP values <0.05). At 48 hours postrun, KFP T2 and PDFF increased; in AT, T1 increased in the INS segment, T2 increased in the INS and MTJ segments (all P values <0.05); PD decreased in all subregions (all P values <0.001). At 2 months, none of the parameters showed significant differences from prerun levels (P>0.05). KFP PDFF change was positively correlated with the change in AT INS T1 (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Marathon running induces reversible microstructural changes in KFP and the AT, and the observed correlations suggest a potential interaction between these structures; SyMRI and IDEAL-IQ enable noninvasive monitoring of these subclinical changes.

articles.title: Fluoroscopy-guided transfemoral pigtail catheter repositioning of malpositioned totally implantable venous access port catheters: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Catheter malposition is a recognized complication of totally implantable venous access ports (TIVAPs). Removal or reimplantation may be unnecessarily invasive when the catheter remains patent, whereas untreated malposition may cause thrombosis, dysfunction, or infusion-related complications. Evidence regarding pigtail catheter repositioning remains limited. This study reviews 39 cases of TIVAP catheter malposition treated using a transfemoral pigtail catheter technique. METHODS: This retrospective case series included 39 patients with imaging-confirmed TIVAP catheter malposition treated between September 2018 and October 2025. Eligible catheters were patent and functional without occlusion; patients with catheter dysfunction or those managed using other repositioning methods were excluded. Under fluoroscopic guidance, a 5-F pigtail catheter was introduced through the femoral vein to redirect the catheter tip into the intended central venous position. RESULTS: The right internal jugular vein was the most common malposition site (25/39, 64.1%). Initial technical success was achieved in all patients, with a mean procedure duration of 13.64±5.02 minutes. No immediate procedure-related complications were documented. Recurrent malposition occurred in 2 patients during a mean follow-up of 3.9±3.7 months (range, 2-14 months). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopy-guided transfemoral pigtail catheter repositioning is technically feasible for selected patients with a functioning, non-occluded malpositioned TIVAP and may avoid immediate catheter replacement or surgical revision.

articles.title: Superiority of magnetic resonance elastography and proton density fat fraction: an umbrella meta-analysis of non-invasive imaging for hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and chronic hepatitis B.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Various quantitative techniques based on ultrasound (US) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) have been widely used to assess hepatic steatosis and fibrosis. This study thus aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the evidence derived from systematic reviews on the diagnostic performance of noninvasive imaging techniques including transient elastography (TE), point shear wave elastography (pSWE), two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE), magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and proton density fat fraction (PDFF) for liver fibrosis and steatosis in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and chronic hepatitis B (CHB). METHODS: Searches were performed on PubMed, Embase, the Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from database inception until 2 March 2025, including keywords 'liver diseases', imaging', 'systematic review' and others. We included systematic reviews that comprised studies evaluating the diagnostic performance of non-invasive imaging techniques for liver fibrosis or steatosis in patients with MASLD or CHB. RESULTS: Thirty-five reviews were included from 3,752 articles. For hepatic steatosis assessment, PDFF demonstrated high diagnostic stability, while CAP showed good screening performance for mild steatosis. For liver fibrosis assessment, MRE exhibited high diagnostic accuracy for significant (≥F2), advanced (≥F3) fibrosis, and cirrhosis (F4). In obese MASLD patients, MRE demonstrated superior specificity compared to TE. Among CHB patients, MRE displayed particularly high diagnostic performance. Other techniques (2D-SWE, TE) remained clinically valuable in specific stages and patient populations. CONCLUSIONS: MRE performance varied between the two etiologies, suggesting liver stiffness is a composite biomarker. PDFF provides precise quantification of steatosis, while CAP is suitable for screening mild cases. The findings emphasize the necessity of developing personalized imaging strategies based on etiology to optimize patient management and reduce reliance on liver biopsy.

articles.title: Lacrimal gland volume changes in unilateral lacrimal drainage obstruction and anophthalmic sockets: a retrospective computed tomography volumetric study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The lacrimal gland (LG), ocular surface, and lacrimal drainage system form an integrated lacrimal functional unit (LFU) that contributes to ocular surface homeostasis. Research on whether lacrimal drainage obstruction (LDO) or an anophthalmic socket is associated with measurable changes in LG volume is limited. This study aimed to evaluate LG volume changes in patients with unilateral LDO or a unilateral anophthalmic socket and to assess whether these structural changes are consistent with altered regulation in the LFU. METHODS: In this retrospective comparative computed tomography (CT) volumetric study, bilateral LG volumes were measured in 11 patients with unilateral congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO), 40 patients with unilateral primary acquired nasolacrimal duct obstruction (PANDO), 24 patients with a unilateral anophthalmic socket, and age-matched imaging controls. LG volumes were compared between the affected side, the contralateral side, and the corresponding control groups. Associations between disease duration and ipsilateral LG volume were assessed using Spearman correlation. RESULTS: Affected-side LG volumes were significantly reduced compared with both the contralateral sides and controls in patients with CNLDO (481.8±164.3 vs. 591.3±172.7 and 631.4±136.7 mm3; P<0.001 and P=0.011), PANDO (399.1±107.5 vs. 465.7±116.5 and 502.8±121.7 mm3; both P<0.001), and an anophthalmic socket (434.9±68.9 vs. 512.0±95.6 mm3, P=0.003; vs. controls, P=0.032). Disease duration was negatively correlated with ipsilateral LG volume in PANDO (r=-0.392, P=0.013) and anophthalmic (r=-0.410, P=0.046) patients. CONCLUSIONS: Unilateral LDO and anophthalmic socket were associated with reduced ipsilateral LG volume compared with both the contralateral side and corresponding controls. Longer disease duration was negatively correlated with ipsilateral LG volume in patients with PANDO and in patients with an anophthalmic socket. These findings suggest that LG morphology may reflect chronic alterations in tear drainage and ocular surface sensory input in the LFU, although the underlying neural mechanisms require further investigation.

articles.title: Threshold effect of post-stenting residual stenosis in severe intracranial stenosis: a post hoc analysis of a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) is a major cause of ischemic stroke. Although intracranial stenting is used in select patients, optimal post-procedural residual stenosis remains unclear. This post hoc analysis aimed to assess the association between post-stenting residual stenosis and 1-year clinical and angiographic outcomes and to explore potential nonlinear and threshold effects. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the NOVA randomized clinical trial included 242 patients with symptomatic 70-99% ICAS who underwent intracranial stenting. Patients were categorized into tertiles according to residual stenosis (T1, n=81; T2, n=80; and T3, n=81). The primary endpoint was a composite of any stroke or death within 30 days or ischemic stroke in the target vessel territory from day 31 to 1 year. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) and piecewise regression analyses were used to explore nonlinear associations and threshold effects. RESULTS: Among 195 patients with evaluable 1-year vascular imaging, in-stent restenosis (ISR) occurred in 9/65 (14%) in the T1 group, 10/65 (15%) in the T2 group, and 22/65 (34%) in the T3 group (P=0.01). A nonlinear relationship was observed between residual stenosis and the composite endpoint (P for overall =0.007; P for nonlinearity =0.03). A threshold effect was identified at 19.94% residual stenosis. Above this threshold, higher residual stenosis was associated with an increased risk of the composite endpoint [hazard ratio (HR) 1.105 per 1% increase; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.037-1.178; P=0.002]. Early (≤30 days) stroke or death tended to be more frequent in the low residual stenosis group, whereas ischemic stroke between 31 days and 1 year occurred more often in patients with high residual stenosis. CONCLUSIONS: Residual stenosis after intracranial stenting showed a nonlinear association with the composite clinical outcome. A threshold was identified at approximately 20%, above which higher residual stenosis was associated with a greater risk of the composite endpoint. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02578069.

articles.title: Deep learning-based super-resolution ultrashort echo time MRI combined with free-breathing Star-VIBE dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI for characterization of Lung-RADS 4 pulmonary nodules.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 4 pulmonary nodules require further evaluation because of indeterminate malignancy risk. However, repeated computed tomography (CT) examinations raise concerns about cumulative radiation exposure, and ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance imaging (UTE-MRI) remains limited by spatial resolution and motion sensitivity. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of generative adversarial network (GAN)-based super-resolution UTE MRI (SR-UTE-MRI) in combination with star-volumetric interpolated breath hold examination (Star-VIBE) dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) for such nodules, using CT and histopathological findings as reference standards. METHODS: In this prospective study, patients with Lung-RADS 4 pulmonary nodules underwent CT, free-breathing UTE-MRI with subsequent SR reconstruction, and Star-VIBE DCE-MRI. Nodule size, morphological features, and perfusion parameters were assessed. Diagnostic performance of individual imaging metrics and a combined model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. A total of 91 patients (43 men and 48 women; mean age, 56.2±13.9 years) with 91 nodules (27 part-solid and 64 solid; mean diameter, 24.1±8.9 mm) were finally included. RESULTS: Measurements derived from UTE-MRI underestimated mean nodule diameter relative to CT, resulting in misclassification in a subset of nodules. SR-UTE-MRI images reduced measurement bias and improved Lung-RADS classification accuracy and visualization of morphological features. Malignant pulmonary nodules demonstrated significantly higher volume transfer constant (Ktrans) and rate constant (Kep) values compared with benign nodules (Ktrans: 0.28 ± 0.19 min-1 vs. 0.16±0.11 min-1, P<0.001; Kep: 0.79±0.38 min-1 vs. 0.53±0.23 min-1,P<0.001). Among individual parameters, Ktrans exhibited the highest diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) =0.799; cut-off, 0.14 min-1]. A multiparametric model incorporating perfusion parameters, nodule size, and spiculation yielded superior discriminatory performance (AUC =0.946; sensitivity =91%; specificity =88%; accuracy =90%). CONCLUSIONS: GAN-based SR-UTE reduced the underestimation of lesion size associated with UTE-MRI and improved the accuracy of Lung-RADS classification. Star-VIBE DCE-MRI provided quantitative functional biomarkers for the assessment of malignancy. The integration of structural and functional imaging parameters yielded superior diagnostic performance compared with single-modality or single-parameter approaches, highlighting its potential as a comprehensive, non-ionizing imaging strategy for evaluation of indeterminate pulmonary nodules.

articles.title: An optimized integrated ultrasound-cardiac magnetic resonance imaging strategy for accurate prenatal diagnosis of fetal aortic arch branch abnormalities: a prospective dual-center study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fetal aortic arch branch abnormalities (FAABAs) are characterized by complex classifications. Accurate prenatal identification and precise sub-typing are of great value for clinical counseling and pregnancy management. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic efficacy of a comprehensive prenatal ultrasound (US) protocol integrating three-vessel and trachea (3VT) view, aortic arch and descending aortic coronal sections (CSs), and four-dimensional (4D) spatiotemporal image correlation combined with high-definition (STIC-HD) live flow imaging. It also compared prenatal US, fetal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI), and combined US + cMRI for diagnosing FAABAs. METHOD: This prospective dual-center study recruited 180 pregnant patients with suspected FAABAs from 2019 to 2021. All underwent three described US examinations, and 33 cases received supplementary fetal cMRI. Postpartum imaging, surgery, and autopsy results were defined as the gold standard. Diagnostic efficiency was validated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, F-score, Youden index, and Cohen's kappa analysis. RESULTS: Gold standard verification identified 165 FAABAs cases (91.7%), including 55.8% left aortic arch, 32.1% right aortic arch, and 12.1% double aortic arch, plus 15 normal cases. The combined 3VT + CS view and comprehensive US protocol yielded a sensitivity of 98.2%, significantly higher than that of single 3VT view (73.5%, P<0.001). The US + cMRI combination achieved the optimal overall diagnostic efficacy (sensitivity: 97.0%, P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: The comprehensive US protocol is the preferred prenatal imaging method for FAABAs diagnosis and classification. Fetal cMRI is a reliable complementary modality, particularly for cases with suboptimal acoustic windows.

articles.title: Quantitative coronary plaque characteristics on coronary computed tomography angiography and their prognostic value in patients with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events. This study compared coronary plaque characteristics assessed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) between patients with and without CKD and evaluated their associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter CREATION-CHINA cohort included patients with suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA during 2016-2020. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Propensity score matching (1:3) used age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, smoking, family history of coronary artery disease, and hyperlipidemia. Quantitative plaque characteristics and perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) were assessed. MACE comprised all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization >90 days after CCTA. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs); analyses of CCTA-derived predictors were adjusted for age, body mass index, and hypertension. High plaque burden was defined as total plaque burden in the highest quartile. RESULTS: After matching, 2,267 patients were included (588 with CKD and 1,679 without CKD). During a median follow-up of 3.47 years (interquartile range, 2.36-4.10), MACE occurred in 30 patients with CKD (5.1%) and 52 without CKD (3.1%; P=0.035). Patients with CKD had higher median total plaque volume (39.90 vs. 0 mm3), median total plaque burden (8.83% vs. 0%), and prevalence of high-risk plaque (9.35% vs. 4.35%; all P<0.001). Among patients with CKD, lipid plaque burden (adjusted HR =1.107, 95% CI: 1.006-1.218; P=0.038) and high FAI (adjusted HR =4.027, 95% CI: 2.329-6.960; P<0.001) were independently associated with MACE. Compared with patients without CKD and with low plaque burden, those with CKD and high plaque burden had a higher risk of MACE (adjusted HR =6.153, 95% CI: 2.937-12.890; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CKD was associated with greater coronary plaque burden and a higher incidence of MACE. Lipid plaque burden and high FAI were independently associated with MACE after adjustment for age, body mass index, and hypertension, supporting their potential role in cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Development of a nomogram integrating contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging radiomics and clinical parameters for differentiating brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma from cerebral tuberculomas.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral tuberculomas and brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma are often indistinguishable on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), leading to misdiagnosis. This study develops a contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics-based nomogram to accurately differentiate them. METHODS: A total of 482 patients (290 males, 192 females; mean age 56.08±12.96 years), including 254 with cerebral tuberculomas and 228 with brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma were enrolled from two centers. Radiomic features were extracted, standardized, and reduced via significance testing, Pearson correlation, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A radiomic model was built, then integrated with clinical predictors into a nomogram. Performance was assessed across training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: A total of 13 radiomic features were selected for model development. The radiomic model demonstrated areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.907, 0.891 and 0.886 in training, internal validation, and independent external validation cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming models based solely on clinical factors, which achieved AUCs of 0.781, 0.712, and 0.828 (P<0.05). The nomogram, which integrated the radiomic scores (Rad-scores), age, ring enhancement, meningeal thickening, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, exhibited superior performance with AUCs of 0.951, 0.937, and 0.940 across the three cohorts. DCA demonstrated that the nomogram provided greater clinical net benefits across a range of threshold probabilities, and calibration curves indicated strong consistency between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A nomogram combining clinical factors and contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics accurately differentiates cerebral tuberculomas from brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma, offering robust decision support for individualized diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Digital subtraction angiography-guided spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis and microsurgical varicocelectomy in the treatment of varicocele: a comparative study with propensity score matching.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Varicocele (VC) adversely affects spermatogenesis and is a recognized contributor to male infertility. This study aimed to compare the safety, efficacy, and clinical value of spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) vs. microsurgical varicocelectomy. METHODS: This retrospective study included 181 patients with VC who were treated from January 2021 to December 2024. After propensity score matching (PSM) at a 1:2 ratio, 38 interventional and 76 surgical patients were included. The interventional group underwent embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA under local anesthesia; the surgical group received microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy under general anesthesia. Postoperative outcomes and semen parameters were compared with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. RESULTS: The interventional group had a significantly shorter procedure duration (52.11±16.97 vs. 67.89±27.91 min, P=0.0003), earlier ambulation [0.47 (0.32, 0.81) vs. 25.06 (24.48, 25.73) h, P<0.001], and shorter hospital stay [2.00 (2.00, 3.75) vs. 3.00 (2.00, 5.00) days, P=0.0173]. Pain relief rates were similar (94.73% vs. 93.42%, P>0.99). The complication rate was numerically lower in the interventional group but did not differ significantly [13.16% (5/38) vs. 28.95% (22/76), P=0.084], with no Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications in either group. At 1-year follow-up, both groups showed significant improvements in all semen parameters (all P<0.001), with no significant between-group differences in the degree of improvement (all P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA may be a safe and effective alternative to microsurgical varicocelectomy, offering faster recovery and comparable semen parameter improvement, particularly for young infertile patients and day-surgery settings, pending further validation.

articles.title: Validation of fully automated myocardial T1 and synthetic hematocrit-based extracellular volume quantification on 3T cardiac MRI: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated post-processing software has been developed to quantify various cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameters, including native T1 and extracellular volume (ECV) using synthetic hematocrit (Hct). However, validation studies of these automated measurements remain limited. We aimed to validate a fully automated workflow integrating myocardial T1 analysis and synthetic Hct for ECV quantification on 3T CMR, using manual ECV calculation based on venous Hct as the reference method. METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 65 adults with low-to-intermediate risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease who underwent stress 3T CMR. Manual ECV was calculated using manually contoured myocardial T1 values and venous Hct obtained within 7 days of CMR. Automated analysis used Myomics-T1 software (Phantomics, Korea) to automatically generate myocardial and blood-pool T1 values and contours, with synthetic Hct derived from a regression model developed in an independent cohort of 450 participants. Correlation and agreement were assessed using Pearson correlation, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: The mean age was 65.2±11.5 years, and 60% of participants were female. Automated myocardial native T1 and ECV showed excellent correlation with manual measurements (r=0.96 and 0.91, respectively) and excellent agreement (ICC =0.96 and 0.93, respectively). Automated myocardial native T1 was slightly higher than manual measurements (1,246±52 vs. 1,233±47 ms), whereas automated ECV was higher by 1.2 percentage points (29.0%±4.9% vs. 27.8%±4.6%). Synthetic Hct correlated with venous Hct (r=0.78; ICC =0.76) but demonstrated proportional bias. Agreement between synthetic Hct-derived and manual ECV was better within the normal Hct range (35-45%) but substantially reduced at Hct >45% (ICC =0.04). CONCLUSIONS: Fully automated ECV quantification demonstrated strong correlation and agreement with the manual method within the normal Hct range. However, synthetic Hct-derived ECV was less reliable at abnormal Hct levels, particularly at Hct >45%. Further external validation and refinement of the synthetic Hct model are warranted to support broader clinical application.

articles.title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. METHODS: Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901) vs. 0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

articles.title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI. METHODS: This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=-0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=-0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=-0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=-0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=-0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=-0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=-0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain. CONCLUSIONS: MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Application of multimodal ultrasound in risk assessment of breast masses: construction and validation of the BI-RADS prediction model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the fact that the diagnosis and treatment levels of breast cancer in first-tier cities have reached international standards and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnosis has been introduced in some regions, economically underdeveloped areas and primary hospitals still face significant bottlenecks in diagnosis and treatment. Standardized risk stratification tools that are tailored to the Chinese population are not yet in common use. Ultrasound, the primary equipment for community breast cancer screening in China, was adopted to develop a simplified quantitative Chinese ultrasound BI-RADS (Breast Imaging-Reporting and Data System) risk stratification model based on the epidemiological features of Chinese breast diseases for precise screening. METHODS: Data of 1,716 patients who underwent ultrasound examination at Ruijin Hospital from August 2019 to September 2020 were collected. The most suspicious lesion identified in each patient was selected for analysis. Taking the ultrasound features of breast masses as independent variables and the pathological benign/malignant status of breast masses as dependent variables, multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed. The regression coefficients were converted to integers as the assigned scores. The total score of each mass was obtained by summing the scores of all indicators, and the malignant rate of masses corresponding to each total score was calculated. The construction of the clinical prediction model for BI-RADS classification involved the implementation of stratification, which was based on the malignant rate of each total score. RESULTS: The following indicators were finally included in the multimodal ultrasound BI-RADS model: ill-defined margin (1 point), spiculation (2 points), microcalcification (2 points), irregular shape (1 point), abundant blood flow (1 point), posterior acoustic shadowing (1 point), and hard strain elastography or maximum shear wave elastography (SWE) ≥87.66 kPa (1 point). The total score ranged from 0 to 8 points, with higher scores, indicating higher malignant rate of the mass. The stratification of multimodal ultrasound BI-RADS was conducted according to the malignant probability. The new model demonstrated high levels of sensitivity and specificity, and was able to effectively differentiate between benign and malignant breast tumors. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.881. CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal ultrasound BI-RADS model provides a novel quantitative method for the risk assessment of breast tumors and has significant clinical application value.

articles.title: Quantitative perfusion analysis of contrast-enhanced ultrasound for the preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion: an experimental study in rabbit VX2 liver tumors.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a critical risk factor for postoperative recurrence and metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, reliable noninvasive preoperative prediction remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate the value of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) in evaluating MVI in rabbit VX2 liver tumors. METHODS: Twenty healthy New Zealand rabbits were selected and used to establish VX2 liver tumor models. After 2 weeks, all models underwent conventional ultrasonography and CEUS with SonoVue (Bracco). We plotted time-intensity curves (TICs) to derive quantitative parameters, including mean intensity of the TIC (mTIC), peak intensity (PI), arrival time (AT), rise time (RT), time to peak (TTP), flow-out time (FT), and mean transit time (mTT). Based on histological diagnosis, tumors were classified into MVI and non-MVI groups. We compared the two groups in terms of the differences between VX2 tumors and the surrounding hepatic parenchyma. RESULTS: (I) Histological examination confirmed that 39 VX2 liver tumor models were successfully established in rabbits, with a tumor inoculation success rate of 97.50%. Among these, MVI was identified in 21 VX2 tumors. (II) Compared to tumors in the non-MVI group, those in the MVI group exhibited a larger diameter (P=0.01). Quantitative CEUS analysis revealed that the MVI group, compared to a non-MVI group, had a higher mTIC and PI (P=0.02 and P<0.001, respectively) and a shorter AT and TTP (both P values =0.03). (III) The RT of VX2 tumors was shorter than that of the surrounding liver parenchyma in both the MVI and non-MVI groups (P=0.002 and P=0.047, respectively). In the MVI group, the AT and TTP of the tumors were shorter (P=0.049 and P<0.001, respectively) while the PI was higher compared to the adjacent parenchyma (P=0.01). (IV) Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that the PI achieved the highest diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve of 0.79 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.65-0.93]. CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative CEUS parameters provide crucial information for evaluating MVI in VX2 liver tumors. These findings constitute experimental evidence that supports the clinical assessment of tumor aggressiveness.

articles.title: Thermographic differentiation of thyroid carcinoma and adenoma in indeterminate cytology nodules: insights from intra- and preoperative imaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Thyroid carcinoma (TC) is the most common endocrine system tumor, whose diagnosis is performed through the fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB), a minimally invasive procedure that uses a thin needle to extract cells from suspicious thyroid nodules for cytological examination. However, in 15-25% of cases there is no certain preoperative response (indeterminate lesions classified as TIR 3A or TIR 3B). In this perspective, developing alternative diagnostic methods is highly desirable. To this aim, infrared thermography (IRT) could be a valuable tool to detect the presence of thyroid cancer. The objective of this study is to investigate the feasibility and the effectiveness of employing IRT to discriminate thyroid cancers in clinical practice. METHODS: The study included 25 participants who underwent to total thyroidectomy surgery: 6 with TC, 5 with thyroid adenoma (TA), and 14 with thyroid goiter (TS). IRT recordings were conducted twice for each patient: first after anesthetic induction with the cervical region exposed and second after intraoperative exposure of the thyroid gland. Two regions of interest (ROIs), corresponding to the right and left thyroid lobes, were analyzed for maximum (Tmax), minimum (Tmin), and average (Tavg) temperatures. The difference between the right and left thyroid lobes sides of the three evaluated metrics was calculated and assessed through t-tests for independent samples. Additionally, the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were calculated to define a threshold for the difference in the considered metrics that distinguishes between subjects with carcinoma, adenoma, and goiter. Finally, a correlation analysis between the inner and external temperature was performed for the three groups. RESULTS: For the cervical region measurements, Tmax successfully distinguished between carcinoma and adenoma (P=0.035) and between goiter and carcinoma (P=0.034). Meanwhile, Tavg showed a significant difference between goiter and carcinoma (P=0.017). For measurements taken on the exposed gland, Tmax could differentiate between carcinoma and adenoma (P=0.044) and between goiter and carcinoma (P=3.81×10⁻4). Tavg was significant in distinguishing goiter from carcinoma (P=0.004) and goiter from adenoma (P=0.028). CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study determined the effectiveness of IRT in identifying thyroid nodular formations suspected of being neoplastic, providing specialists and patients with an additional diagnostic tool for managing thyroid nodules, especially those cytologically characterized as indeterminate risk neoplastic lesions. IRT could represent a valid complementary tool that may assist the physician in the diagnostic process of thyroid nodules.

articles.title: Dual context attentive feature network: an interpretable dual-pathway deep learning framework for accurate gastrointestinal endoscopic image classification.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases such as colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) contribute substantially to global morbidity, with colorectal cancer accounting for nearly 10% of all cancer diagnoses worldwide. Many existing artificial intelligence (AI) models suffer from limited generalizability and poor clinical interpretability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an explainable AI (XAI) framework for classifying GI diseases from endoscopic images. METHODS: Public datasets from the Simula Research Laboratory were used: Hyper-Kvasir (10,662 images) for training, Kvasir-V1 (4,000 images) for validation, and Kvasir-V2 (8,000 images) as an independent test set. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, GastroNet-dilated multi-scale attention (DMSA) (a proposed DMSA Network) and M2ShallowNet (a lightweight hybrid model), were designed for complementary feature extraction. Deep features were fused using a dual context attentive feature network (DCAF-Net) followed by Aquila Optimizer (AO)-based feature-weight refinement without introducing additional trainable fusion parameters. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and statistical testing. Interpretability was examined using gradient-weighted class activation mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). RESULTS: The best-performing classifier, a multilayer perceptron (MLP), achieved an accuracy of 97.21%, precision of 97.27%, recall of 97.21%, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.82%, and F1-score of 97.21% on the independent test set. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent class separability, and statistical testing confirmed reliable generalization. XAI results highlighted regions that qualitatively correspond to pathological areas; formal clinical validation of these interpretations was not performed in this study. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework offers a promising research prototype for AI-assisted GI disease classification. Its potential for real-world endoscopic deployment requires further prospective validation before clinical adoption.

articles.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion imaging for characterizing angiogenesis in soft-tissue sarcomas: an exploratory study based on MRI-pathology co-alignment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression and microvessel density (MVD) are established markers of tumor angiogenesis and key targets for anti-angiogenic therapy in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs). Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) imaging are complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods commonly used to assess angiogenesis in a variety of tumors. This study aimed to explore whether DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging could be used as non-invasive tools to evaluate tumor angiogenesis in STS based on MRI-pathology co-alignment. METHODS: In total, 70 patients with STS underwent 3.0-T DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging. The volume transfer constant (Ktrans), reflux rate constant (Kep), volume fraction of the extravascular extracellular space (Ve), true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f) were measured. Correlations between MRI parameters and VEGF expression or MVD were examined. Differences in MRI parameters between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and interobserver reproducibility was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). An MRI-pathology control protocol was implemented to verify the spatial correspondence between MRI slices and their corresponding histologic sections. RESULTS: Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f were positively correlated with VEGF expression (r=0.673, 0.573, 0.692, and 0.386, respectively) and MVD (r=0.662, 0.595, 0.619, and 0.344, respectively). Ktrans and D* were identified as independent factors associated with VEGF expression and MVD. No significant correlations were observed between Ve or D and either angiogenesis marker. Tumors with high VEGF expression exhibited higher Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f values than those with low VEGF expression. The areas under the ROC curves for the four parameters in differentiating between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were 0.861, 0.844, 0.860, and 0.720, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrated associations between DCE-MRI- and IVIM-derived perfusion metrics and VEGF expression and MVD in STSs.

articles.title: Residual CatLet score predicts the long-term prognosis in "all-comers" patients with coronary artery disease: a survival analysis study based on time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In recent years, the incidence and mortality rates of coronary artery disease (CAD) have been rising annually. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of the coronary artery tree description and lesion evaluation (CatLet) angiographic scoring system to stratify risk and to elucidate its independent prognostic value in "all-comers" patients with CAD.
