METHODS: A total of 373 consecutive CAD patients were enrolled at The First People's Hospital of Hefei following coronary angiography. The residual CatLet (rCatLet) score was calculated based on the residual lesions after completion of required revascularization at physicians' discretion during this hospitalization for all enrolled patients, who subsequently underwent follow-ups. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Secondary endpoints included all-cause death and cardiac death. Survival rates were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic factors, while the prognostic value of the rCatLet score was evaluated by the time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC). RESULTS: This was a single-center cohort study of 279 patients, including 56 (20.07%) with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and 223 (79.93%) with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed progressively worse prognosis across higher rCatLet score tertiles for all endpoints (all log-rank P<0.001). Cox regression revealed that, compared with the low tertile, the highest rCatLet tertile was associated with a significantly increased risk of MACCEs [hazard ratio (HR) =4.96; 95% confidence interval (CI): 3.03-8.12], and the medium tertile showed a non-significant trend toward higher risk (HR =1.39; 95% CI: 0.79-2.43). Time-dependent ROC analysis showed that the rCatLet model predicted 1-, 3-, and 6-year MACCEs with AUCs (95% CIs) of 0.85 (0.77-0.92), 0.73 (0.64-0.81), and 0.71 (0.64-0.77). The multivariable-adjusted models performed better, and their AUCs (95% CIs) at the three time points were 0.87 (0.83-0.92), 0.78 (0.72-0.86), and 0.78 (0.73-0.84), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Our exploratory findings suggest that the rCatLet score has predictive value for the short- and long-term clinical prognosis in "all-comers" patients with CAD. Furthermore, the rCatLet score adjusted for clinical variables showed improved prognostic predictive values. These findings require further validation in future studies.

articles.title: Association of computed tomography-derived vascular indices with shock and blood transfusion in blunt abdominal trauma: a structural equation modeling approach.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypovolemic shock and blood transfusion requirement are critical early outcomes in blunt abdominal trauma. Conventional clinical parameters may underestimate physiological compromise, particularly in occult shock. Computed tomography (CT)-derived vascular indices, including inferior vena cava (IVC) morphology and IVC-to-aorta ratios, have been proposed as complementary imaging biomarkers of volume depletion, yet evidence on which specific metrics best predict these outcomes remains inconsistent. This study aimed to identify CT-derived vascular metrics associated with shock and blood transfusion requirements in adults with blunt abdominal trauma, and to evaluate their added value when integrated with clinical indicators within a holistic diagnostic framework. METHODS: Consecutive adult patients with blunt abdominal trauma who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT within three hours of arrival were retrospectively included. Epidemiological and clinical data were collected. IVC (minimum, maximum diameters, and area) at four levels (hepatic, suprarenal, juxtarenal, infrarenal) and aorta diameters were measured. Logistic regression identified predictors of shock at presentation and blood transfusion within the first 24 hours, while structural equation modeling (SEM) elucidated structural relationships among clinical and CT-derived vascular variables associated with blood transfusion. RESULTS: A total of 190 patients (mean age 39.8±15.1 years; 151 men) were included, 49 (25.8%) with shock and 79 (41.6%) requiring blood transfusion. Median Abbreviated Injury Scale-Abdomen (AIS-Abdomen) was 3 (range, 0-5), and median Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 22 (range, 4-75). Small infrarenal IVC area <1.5 cm2 and aorta diameter <1.5 cm was linked to higher odds of shock (odds ratio: 2.979-4.717, P=0.002-0.010). A lower suprarenal IVC/aorta ratio was associated with a higher likelihood of transfusion (odds ratio: 0.211, P=0.026) along with higher heart rate, ISS, AIS-Abdomen, and prothrombin time (PT). The final SEM model explained 70.5% of the variance (R2=0.705) and identified four contributory pathways to blood transfusion, three of which reached statistical significance, with the coagulopathy pathway showing a non-significant trend (P=0.075). CONCLUSIONS: Infrarenal IVC area and aorta diameter were significantly associated with shock, whereas the suprarenal IVC/aorta ratio was associated with blood transfusion requirement. These CT-derived vascular indices provide independent predictive value for shock and blood transfusion when integrated with clinical parameters, supporting a comprehensive quadruple driver model for trauma resuscitation in which transfusion decisions arise from the interaction of four key domains: (I) anatomical injury burden, represented by ISS; (II) hemodynamic instability, represented by shock status and heart rate; (III) coagulopathy, represented by PT; and (IV) radiological hypovolemia, represented by the suprarenal IVC/aorta ratio. As a relative index that compensates for individual body habitus and physiological variability, the suprarenal IVC/aorta ratio is prioritized over absolute IVC dimensions within this framework, supporting safer and more robust clinical application in trauma resuscitation.

articles.title: Age-group differences in the N170 response during Chinese character processing in children aged 7-11 years: a cross-sectional event-related potential study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Research on age-related changes in early electrophysiological responses to Chinese print across primary-school years is limited. This study examined age-group differences in the N170 response during Chinese character processing in children aged 7-11 years. METHODS: A total of 103 children aged 7-11 years completed a semantic priming and pseudocharacter judgment task during electroencephalographic recording. Mean N170 voltage was measured from 130 to 240 ms at P7 and P8, the posterior occipitotemporal electrodes. A linear mixed-effects model was used to examine the effects of age group, stimulus type, and hemisphere, as well as their interactions, with sex and the sex-by-hemisphere interaction included as additional fixed effects. A generalized estimating equation (GEE) model was used for the sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Mean voltage in the N170 window differed across age groups [Wald χ2(4) =20.75, P<0.001]. Values were lower in 7-year-olds than in 10- and 11-year-olds (both Holm-adjusted P<0.001). Stimulus type (P=0.082) and hemisphere (P=0.152) were not significant, and neither showed a reliable interaction with age group. The three-way interaction, sex effect, and sex-by-hemisphere interaction were also nonsignificant. The sensitivity analysis yielded comparable results. CONCLUSIONS: N170-window mean voltage differed by age group, with the clearest differences between the 7-year-old group and the 10- and 11-year-old groups. No evidence of discrete transition windows or an age-related hemispheric shift was found. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine how these responses develop across childhood.

articles.title: A new perspective on dysplastic spondylolisthesis: imaging analysis and hypothesis on the pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysplastic spondylolisthesis (DS) is a common spine disease in children and adolescents, and its pathogenesis remains unclear. Few previous studies have focused on the cauda equina in patients with DS. This retrospective case-control study evaluated the imaging findings of patients with DS from a novel perspective and attempted to speculate on its underlying etiology. METHODS: 126 young patients (16-24 years) with DS were selected, and the lumbar spinal canal ratio (LSCR) and disc height index (DHI) of nondiseased segments (L1-L5) were measured. The morphology of the cauda equina was observed via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We also measured the filum terminale detection rate (FTDR), filum terminale diameter (FTD), and the relative position of the conus medullaris on MRI. The DS group was compared with the control group. The control group consisted of 126 healthy young individuals who were age- and sex-matched to the DS group. RESULTS: Compared with that in the control group, the cauda equina in the DS group was more likely to experience excessive posterior displacement (EPD) (P<0.05). DS patients showed a lower FTDR and smaller FTD at the L4-L5 and L5-S1 segments (P<0.05), and exhibited a higher conus medullaris position (P<0.05). The LSCR in L3-L5 segments was significantly greater in the DS group than in the control group (P<0.05). There was no significant difference in the DHI between the two groups at all lumbar segments. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with healthy young individuals, patients with DS demonstrate thinner filum terminale, a relatively higher position of the conus medullaris, a wider spinal canal, and a higher incidence of cauda equina EPD. Based on these imaging differences, we explored the potential causes of DS and put forward the compensatory spondylolisthesis hypothesis.

articles.title: Spatial correspondence between spontaneous brain activity alterations and normative molecular and neurochemical architecture in pediatric epilepsy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric epilepsy is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed brain networks, but the molecular context of spontaneous brain activity alterations remains incompletely understood. This study investigated regional spontaneous brain activity alterations in pediatric epilepsy and their spatial correspondence with normative molecular reference maps. METHODS: In this observational case-control neuroimaging study, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data from 44 children with epilepsy and 44 healthy controls selected using group-level frequency matching for age and sex were analyzed. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional ALFF (fALFF) were compared between groups. The unthresholded signed ALFF case-control t-map was subsequently parcellated using the Schaefer 2018 400-parcel atlas. The 200 left-hemisphere cortical parcels were spatially related to normative adult Allen Human Brain Atlas gene-expression data using partial least squares (PLS) regression, and the whole-cortex ALFF map was compared with 39 normative adult neurotransmitter maps. RESULTS: First partial least squares component (PLS1) explained 36.42% of the variance in the left-hemisphere cortical ALFF map and was significant under 10,000 spherical spin permutations (P_spin=0.0004); regional PLS1 scores were positively associated with ALFF t-values (ρ=0.5650, P_spin=0.0004). PLS1-associated genes were enriched for synaptic, ion-transport, membrane-regulation, and neuronal-projection annotations, and inhibitory-neuron gene sets showed significant enrichment (P=0.0014). The signed ALFF map showed inverse spatial associations with the MU_CARFENTANIL_c11 μ-opioid receptor map (median Spearman ρ=-0.3317, mean Fisher z=-0.3448, P_spin=0.0003, q_FDR =0.0044) and the mGluR5_abp_hc73_smart map (median Spearman ρ=-0.2610, mean Fisher z=-0.2672, P_spin=0.0001, q_FDR =0.0022). CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide indirect atlas-based spatial molecular context for the pediatric imaging phenotype. Because the molecular maps were derived from independent adult reference datasets, the associations should not be interpreted as patient-specific gene-expression or receptor measurements, causal mechanisms, or developmentally matched molecular abnormalities.

articles.title: MRI abnormalities of tarsal tunnel contents in symptomatic adolescent and young adult patients with talocalcaneal coalition.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescent and young adult patients with talocalcaneal coalition (TCC) frequently suffer from recurrent ankle sprains and chronic medial hindfoot pain. Given that TCC may exert variable impacts on tarsal tunnel contents, this study aimed to investigate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities of tarsal tunnel contents in this patient population. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on MRI data of 124 symptomatic adolescent and young adult patients with TCC. TCC lesions were classified according to anatomical location, tissue type, and morphological characteristics. MRI abnormalities of tarsal tunnel contents, including the flexor hallucis longus tendon (FHLT), flexor digitorum longus tendon (FDLT), posterior tibial tendon (PTT), and medial plantar nerve (MPN), were evaluated and their differences were compared. Patients were stratified into abnormal and corresponding normal subgroups based on the MRI findings of the FHLT, FDLT, PTT, and MPN, and inter-group differences in the incidence of various clinical manifestations were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 124 subjects (84 males, median age 23 years), FHLT abnormalities were identified in 66 cases (53.2%), FDLT abnormalities in 22 (17.7%), PTT abnormalities in 6 (4.8%), and MPN abnormalities in 71 (57.3%). No significant difference was observed in FHLT abnormality among the three anatomical types (intra-articular, extra-articular, and mixed type; P>0.05). The rates of FDLT and MPN abnormalities in intra-articular TCC were significantly lower than those in extra-articular and mixed TCC (all P<0.05). No significant difference in PTT abnormality was found between intra-articular and extra-articular TCC (P>0.05), whereas the rate of PTT abnormality was significantly lower in intra-articular TCC than in mixed TCC (P=0.005). Notably, no significant differences in FHLT, FDLT, PTT or MPN abnormalities were observed among TCCs with different tissue types (osseous, fibrous or cartilaginous) or morphological characteristics (types I-IV) (all P>0.05). The prevalence of recurrent sprains with medial ankle pain was significantly higher in the FDLT-abnormal and MPN-abnormal groups than in their respective normal counterparts (P<0.05). For hindfoot stiffness with restricted mobility and symptom exacerbation by activity/prolonged standing and relief with rest, their prevalences were statistically significantly increased in the FHLT-abnormal and MPN-abnormal groups relative to the corresponding normal groups (P<0.05). Associated tarsal tunnel syndrome (TTS) manifesting as plantar numbness or paresthesia and hindfoot valgus were significantly more frequent in all four tendon/nerve abnormal subgroups (FHLT, FDLT, PTT, MPN) compared with normal groups (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic adolescent and young adult patients with TCC are frequently associated with abnormalities to the tarsal tunnel contents, and MPN abnormality is the most common, followed by FHLT abnormality. Extra-articular and mixed-type TCCs are more likely to cause MPN and FDLT abnormalities.

articles.title: Combined quantitative speed-of-sound imaging and shear-wave elastography for differentiating benign and malignant breast lesions: development of a multimodal ultrasound nomogram.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate differentiation of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for guiding clinical management and reducing unnecessary biopsies. However, conventional ultrasound alone often has limited specificity. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of shear-wave elastography (SWE) and quantitative speed-of-sound (QSOS) imaging and to develop a multimodal ultrasound nomogram integrating quantitative imaging parameters with conventional ultrasound features for breast lesion characterization. METHODS: This retrospective study included 108 breast lesions (43 malignant and 65 benign) from 108 women who underwent conventional B-mode ultrasound, SWE, and QSOS imaging before histopathological confirmation. Quantitative SWE and QSOS parameters were obtained from intralesional and perilesional regions. Imaging predictors associated with malignancy were selected through least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and subsequently evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Independent predictors were incorporated into a diagnostic nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, DeLong test, calibration curves, bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions) for internal validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: Malignant lesions exhibited significantly higher maximum elasticity (Emax) and QSOS values than benign lesions [Emax: 70.6±33.5 vs. 40.9±21.4 kPa; QSOS: 1,557.1 (1,535.8-1,564.9) vs. 1,529.7 (1,506.1-1,543.9) m/s; both P<0.001]. Multivariable analysis identified lesion size [odds ratio (OR) =1.12, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.02-1.26, P=0.030], non-parallel orientation (OR =18.93, 95% CI: 2.00-303.26, P=0.019), calcification (OR =20.18, 95% CI: 3.44-187.76, P=0.002), Emax (OR =1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.10, P=0.007), and QSOS per 10 m/s increase (OR =1.71, 95% CI: 1.13-2.93, P=0.024) as independent predictors of malignancy. QSOS and Emax showed moderate diagnostic performance, with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.776 and 0.775, respectively, whereas their combination improved the AUC to 0.850 (95% CI: 0.774-0.926). The multimodal nomogram integrating conventional ultrasound features, Emax, and QSOS achieved excellent discrimination (AUC =0.969; 95% CI: 0.943-0.994), with 88.4% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity. The nomogram significantly outperformed the conventional ultrasound model alone according to the DeLong test (P=0.030) and demonstrated favorable calibration and clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: SWE and QSOS provide complementary quantitative information for breast lesion characterization. Integration of conventional ultrasound features with quantitative stiffness and sound-speed information in a multimodal nomogram demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance and may provide a quantitative adjunctive approach for improving breast lesion assessment and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Quantitative analysis of motion-induced dose uncertainty and robust optimization in liver lattice radiotherapy: a comparative study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The precise delivery of high doses to lattice vertices in liver lattice radiotherapy (LRT) can be compromised by respiratory motion.This study aimed to quantitatively characterize the dosimetric impact of respiratory motion on liver LRT and to assess the potential of four-dimensional (4D) robust optimization in mitigating motion-induced uncertainties. METHODS: Twenty-one patients with bulky liver tumors underwent 4D computed tomography scanning. Three lattice target volumes (LTVs) were generated using varied lattice geometries defined by vertex sizes and spacing. Conventional and 4D robust plans were generated on average intensity projection images. Four-dimensional dose distributions were reconstructed via deformable image registration-based dose accumulation across all respiratory phases. Dosimetric parameters of LTVs and organs at risk (OARs) were compared between static three-dimensional (3D) and dynamic 4D scenarios. Spearman correlation coefficients were calculated to quantify the relationship between motion amplitudes and dosimetric variations. RESULTS: Respiratory motion introduced substantial dose degradation in conventional plans. Specifically, LTV Dmin and D98, which represent the minimum dose and the dose covering 98% of the structure, decreased by up to 12.71% and 9.45%, respectively. Motion amplitude was strongly correlated with dose deviations (r>0.7). In contrast, 4D robust plans significantly improved dose stability, with discrepancies in Dmin and D98 between 3D and 4D dose metrics reduced to within 1.4%. Robust optimization led to a significant decrease in the conformity index (CI) in 3D scenarios, but the CI of these robust plans significantly improved in 4D evaluations (P<0.01). Furthermore, under 4D evaluation, robust plans maintained clinically acceptable target conformity, with no statistically significant differences observed compared to conventional plans in most configurations. OAR doses remained within clinically acceptable limits for both conventional and robust plans. CONCLUSIONS: Liver LRT is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, resulting in notable target dose deterioration under conventional planning. Four-dimensional robust optimization demonstrated the ability to address motion-induced uncertainties and facilitate robust target coverage while maintaining favorable conformity in 4D scenarios through necessary high-dose volume expansion. These findings highlight the importance of integrating motion-aware optimization and patient-specific motion management strategies in clinical LRT planning.

articles.title: Study on the topological features of cortical morphological similarity networks in Alzheimer's disease of different cognitive states.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Individual morphological similarity networks (MSNs) were constructed based on cortical morphological metrics extracted from structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) data to investigate topological abnormalities in brain structural networks in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their correlations with cognitive levels. METHODS: Based on T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images from 83 AD patients and 40 healthy controls (HC), we extracted gray matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness (CT), and surface area (SA). Individual MSNs were constructed by calculating the Pearson correlation coefficients between the three-dimensional morphometric feature vectors of pairs of cortical regions. Graph theoretical analysis was then employed to compute nodal topological metrics, including betweenness centrality (Bc), degree centrality (Dc), nodal efficiency (Ne), and nodal local efficiency (Nle), to identify abnormal alterations in the brain structural networks of AD patients. Furthermore, we explored the correlations between mini-mental state examination (MMSE) scores and these altered nodal topological metrics. Based on their MMSE scores, AD patients were further categorized into high cognitive (high-MMSE) and low cognitive (low-MMSE) subgroups. Finally, topological metrics showing significant differences between the AD and HC groups were compared across the high-MMSE, low-MMSE and HC groups. RESULTS: Significant MSN topological alterations in AD were predominantly localized in the frontal regions. Dc was generally reduced in the frontal regions of AD patients, including the bilateral middle frontal gyrus (P=0.027; P=0.007) and bilateral superior frontal gyrus (P=0.007; P=0.020). MMSE scores correlated positively with Dc in the right transverse frontopolar gyri and sulci (r=0.335, P=0.03) but negatively with Dc (r=-0.352, P=0.03) and Ne (r=-0.324, P=0.03) in the right superior frontal sulcus. The low-MMSE group exhibited lower Dc in the left middle frontal gyrus (P=0.0167) and left superior frontal gyrus (P=0.0008) than HCs, with a trend toward lower values compared with the high-MMSE group. Conversely, the high-MMSE group showed significantly lower Dc (P=0.002) and Ne (P=0.0142) in the right superior frontal sulcus than the low-MMSE group. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that AD patients exhibit structural network alterations predominantly involving frontal regions, with characteristic patterns corresponding to cognitive severity. These MSN topological alterations may provide insights into the network mechanisms underlying cognitive heterogeneity in AD and highlight the potential of network-based measures for characterizing disease-related brain alterations.

articles.title: Automated quantitative computed tomography grading of lumbar facet joint degeneration: influence of segmentation errors on instance-level clinical assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated lumbar facet joint degeneration grading requires both accurate anatomical segmentation and clinically meaningful region-level classification. We evaluated whether voxel-level segmentation performance was aligned with downstream degeneration grading. METHODS: This retrospective study included 145 lumbar computed tomography (CT) examinations and 725 level-specific bilateral facet joint regions of interest (ROIs), including 165 severe and 560 non-severe regions. Weishaupt grades 0-1 were categorized as non-severe and grades 2-3 as severe. Scheme A used binary nnU-Net segmentation followed by 11 quantitative region-level features, training-fold-specific standardization, and logistic regression; an oracle comparison using ground-truth masks was compared with analysis using predicted masks. Scheme B used direct three-class segmentation. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation was performed, with 116 training and 29 validation patients per fold. The results were reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD). RESULTS: Scheme A achieved a binary segmentation Dice coefficient of 0.770±0.008. In the oracle comparison, the region-level area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), recall, F1-score, accuracy, and case-level accuracy were 0.671±0.100, 0.538±0.172, 0.399±0.102, 0.640±0.051, and 0.579±0.096, respectively. Using predicted masks, the corresponding values were 0.650±0.068, 0.603±0.250, 0.375±0.072, 0.563±0.123, and 0.545±0.071. Scheme B achieved a native nnU-Net mean validation Dice of 0.493±0.044 and region-level AUC, recall, F1-score, accuracy, and case-level accuracy of 0.730±0.024, 0.445±0.051, 0.510±0.045, 0.808±0.015, and 0.738±0.058, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Voxel-level segmentation and clinically oriented grading performance were not directly aligned. Scheme A provided stable anatomical segmentation but more variable downstream grading, whereas scheme B achieved better overall region- and case-level classification performance but lower severe-degeneration recall. Both spatial and clinical decision metrics should therefore be considered when evaluating automated facet joint grading systems.

articles.title: Image quality and radiation dose optimization in CT pulmonary angiography using 120, 100, and 80 kV protocols for pulmonary thromboembolism diagnosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the standard imaging modality for diagnosing pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE). Lowering tube potential enhances iodine attenuation but may affect image noise. This retrospective study evaluated quantitative image quality, subjective ratings, and radiation dose across 120, 100, and 80 kV CTPA protocols on a dual-source CT scanner. METHODS: Ninety adult patients (n=30 per protocol) undergoing clinically indicated CTPA were evaluated across three tube potential settings (120, 100, and 80 kV). Quantitative parameters pulmonary artery attenuation [Hounsfield unit (HU)], image noise [standard deviation (SD)], signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and size-specific dose estimates (SSDE)-were evaluated. Three cardiothoracic radiologists performed blinded qualitative assessments using a 5-point Likert scale. Radiation dose metrics [volumetric computed tomography dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and estimated effective dose] were recorded. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics [age, sex, body mass index (BMI)] were comparable across groups (P>0.05). Pulmonary artery attenuation increased significantly as tube potential decreased, reaching highest values at 80 kV (633.9±92.1 vs. 338.5±42.1 HU at 120 kV, P<0.001). Image noise increased modestly at 80 kV (25.88±5.0 vs. 20.23±4.1 HU, P=0.26). SNR and CNR were significantly higher at 80 kV (25.93±2.6 and 25.20±3.4) compared with 120 kV (18.19±4.8 and 9.31±2.1, P<0.001). Effective dose decreased significantly by 46.4% from 3.34±0.67 mSv (120 kV) to 1.79±0.35 mSv (80 kV) (P<0.001). Qualitative scores for overall image quality, vascular enhancement, and motion artifacts showed no significant differences across protocols (P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Lowering tube potential to 80 kV in CTPA significantly increases vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR while offering substantial radiation dose savings and maintaining subjective image quality scores. These findings support the feasibility of an 80-kV protocol for radiation dose optimization in CTPA.

articles.title: MIFF-CLIP-HCC: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining-enhanced multimodal information fusion framework for early recurrence prediction in postoperative hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common malignant tumors in China, and its prognosis is affected by many factors, such as tumor stage, liver function status, and patient health. To formulate treatment plans and evaluate prognosis, clinicians require accurate prediction of early postoperative recurrence of HCC. To address this clinical need, this study proposes a novel deep learning framework, termed MIFF-CLIP-HCC, to predict the early postoperative recurrence of HCC based on multimodal information fusion framework (MIFF) and Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP). METHODS: The MIFF-CLIP-HCC framework comprises two core steps. It first uses a fusion framework with a bidirectional attention mechanism to integrate multimodal information, including arterial phase images, venous phase images, and clinical data from patients with HCC. It then introduces image features extracted by the foundational CLIP model to deeply mine effective information from arterial and venous phase images, which increases the performance of the model. RESULTS: Between 2022 and 2025, a total of 240 early-stage HCC patients from two centers were included. Of these, 180 were from The First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (Center 1) (including 114 early recurrence cases and 66 non-early recurrence cases, with an 8:2 ratio for training and internal testing), and the remaining 60 were from Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (Center 2) (including 35 early recurrence cases and 25 non-early recurrence cases), designated as the external test cohort. The accuracy and robustness of the model were validated on internal and external test sets. The model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.844 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.726-0.963] on the internal test set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.651-0.867) on the external test set, outperforming other fusion frameworks (best baseline AUC: 0.779 on internal and 0.690 on external). CONCLUSIONS: The results demonstrate that the proposed MIFF-CLIP-HCC framework, which employs dual optimization strategies of multimodal information fusion and CLIP, significantly improves the accuracy of early postoperative recurrence prediction for HCC, thus demonstrating considerable potential for clinical application.

articles.title: Value of left atrial to left ventricular volume ratio in left heart remodeling classification and postoperative prognosis assessment in patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) patients exhibit heterogeneous left heart remodeling, with unclear impacts on postoperative prognosis. This study aimed to classify left heart remodeling subtypes using the left atrial (LA) to left ventricular (LV) volume ratio, analyze subtype differences, and validate the ratio's predictive value for 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective study included 350 RMS patients who underwent mitral valve surgery between February 2021 and October 2024. Preoperative LA end-systolic volume (LAESV) and LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) were measured by three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography to calculate the LA/LV volume ratio. The optimal cutoff value was determined by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Patients were divided into predominantly LV remodeling (PLVR) and predominantly LA remodeling (PLAR) groups. Clinical data, echocardiographic parameters, and 1-year adverse outcomes [a composite of heart failure (HF) rehospitalization and all-cause mortality] were compared. Risk factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses. RESULTS: The LA/LV volume ratio yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.723 (P<0.001) for predicting 1-year adverse outcomes, with an optimal cutoff of 0.61. PLAR patients (LA/LV >0.61, n=168) were older, more frequently female, had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), more severe mitral stenosis, and larger right atrial volume (all P<0.001). PLVR patients (LA/LV ≤0.61, n=182) had a higher rate of ischemic heart disease, lower LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and a higher proportion of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (all P<0.001). The 1-year composite adverse event rate was 20.6% overall, significantly higher in the PLAR group than in the PLVR group (34.3% vs. 15.1%, P<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression identified PLAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.72, P=0.008], preoperative N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >3,000 pg/mL (HR =1.91, P=0.002), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV (HR =2.15, P=0.002), moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (HR =1.58, P=0.036), and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR =1.63, P=0.029) as independent risk factors. CONCLUSIONS: The LA/LV volume ratio (optimal cutoff 0.61) effectively classifies RMS left heart remodeling subtypes. PLAR is associated with increased 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes, and integrating mitral/tricuspid regurgitation assessment and extended echocardiographic parameters enhances prognostic accuracy. This provides a robust tool for preoperative risk stratification and individualized treatment in RMS patients.

articles.title: Qualitative contrast-enhanced ultrasound alone for thyroid nodule characterization and the lack of incremental diagnostic value of quantitative parameters: a single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The added value of quantitative contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) parameters in thyroid nodule (TN) evaluation remains uncertain. This study investigated whether quantitative CEUS parameters provide any incremental diagnostic benefit over B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) combined with qualitative CEUS in differentiating benign from malignant TNs for reducing unnecessary fine-needle aspiration biopsies (FNABs). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 350 pathologically confirmed TNs from 308 consecutive patients examined at a tertiary hospital between December 2019 and March 2023. Two blinded radiologists scored BMUS features according to the 2017 American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) lexicon and assessed qualitative CEUS features, including enhancement direction, enhancement pattern, peak enhancement intensity, and ring enhancement. Quantitative lesion-to-parenchyma ratios determined from time-intensity curves (TICs) included those related to peak intensity (PI), wash-in and wash-out area under the curve (AUC), mean transit time (mTTI), and time to peak (TTP). Three multivariable logistic models were built: BMUS alone, BMUS plus qualitative CEUS, and BMUS plus both qualitative and quantitative CEUS. The AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values were calculated for the three models. The AUCs were then compared between BMUS and BMUS plus qualitative CEUS, between BMUS and BMUS plus qualitative and quantitative CEUS, and between BMUS plus qualitative CEUS and BMUS plus qualitative and quantitative CEUS. Subgroup analyses were performed based on ACR TI-RADS level (4 vs. 5), nodule size (<1 vs. ≥1 cm), and composition (solid vs. mixed cystic-solid). RESULTS: Of the 350 nodules, 245 (70.0%) were malignant. For the whole cohort, the AUCs yielded by the models composed of BMUS alone, BMUS plus qualitative CEUS, and BMUS plus both qualitative and quantitative CEUS were 0.793 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.750-0.837], 0.830 (95% CI: 0.787-0.868), and 0.821 (95% CI:0.777-0.860), respectively, with no significant pairwise difference (P=0.072, P=0.231, and P=0.620). Adding qualitative CEUS to BMUS raised the AUC in ACR TI-RADS 4 nodules (0.691 to 0.834; P=0.004), nodules ≥1 cm (0.810 to 0.865; P=0.020) and mixed cystic-solid nodules (0.714 to 0.862, P=0.014), whereas adding quantitative parameters to BMUS plus qualitative CEUS produced no further gain in any subgroup (all P values >0.05). Among ACR TI-RADS 4-5 nodules with a diameter ≥1 cm, the unnecessary-FNAB rate fell from 35.9% with ACR TI-RADS to 15.9% with BMUS plus qualitative CEUS (P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, qualitative CEUS combined with BMUS was sufficient for effective TN characterization, with the most benefit in ACR TI-RADS 4, ≥1 cm, and mixed cystic-solid nodules, whereas quantitative parameters added no incremental diagnostic value. Prospective multicenter validation is required before quantitative analysis can be omitted in routine practice.

articles.title: Clinical significance of myocardial layer-specific ventricular-arterial coupling index in community populations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traditional global indices of ventricular-arterial coupling (VAC) often fail to reflect regional myocardial mechanics. The aim of this study was to establish and validate novel layer-specific artery-myocardial strain coupling indices by integrating arterial stiffness with layer-specific global circumferential strains (GCSs), and to determine the clinical significance of these layer-specific VAC indices across different age groups. METHODS: Left ventricular (LV) structural and functional parameters-including conventional indices and layer-specific GCSs for the endomyocardial, midmyocardial, and epimyocardial (GCSendo, GCSmid, and GCSepi) layers assessed via two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE)-were analyzed in 398 community-dwelling individuals stratified by age, gender, and body mass index (BMI). Arterial stiffness was quantified using the arterial velocity pulse index (AVI). Layer-specific VAC indices were mathematically defined as the ratio of AVI to each layer's GCS (AVI/GCSendo, AVI/GCSmid, and AVI/GCSepi). Multiple linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of these coupling ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to compare the diagnostic performance between novel and traditional VAC indices. RESULTS: The AVI/GCSendo, AVI/GCSmid, and AVI/GCSepi ratios progressively decreased from young to older individuals (r=-0.466, -0.453, and -0.375; all P<0.001), with no significant differences observed across gender or BMI strata. Correlation analyses revealed that all three ratios were significantly correlated with age and LV ejection fraction (LVEF); furthermore, AVI/GCSmid showed additional correlation with tissue Doppler imaging e' velocity (TDI e'), whereas AVI/GCSepi correlated with heart rate (HR). Multivariate regression confirmed that age and LVEF were independent predictors of these coupling ratios. Moreover, ROC curve analyses demonstrated that the diagnostic performance of AVI/GCSendo, AVI/GCSmid, and AVI/GCSepi significantly surpassed that of traditional VAC indices, such as ventricular-vascular coupling index (VVI), across all age strata. CONCLUSIONS: Independently determined by age and LVEF, the novel layer-specific AVI/GCS indices are significantly superior to traditional VVI in detecting age-related impairments in cardiovascular function. By revealing distinct transmural functional heterogeneity across myocardial layers, these indices offer a multidimensional framework for evaluating age-related cardiovascular functional alterations.

articles.title: Platform-driven multidisciplinary integration for graduate medical imaging education: a theoretical framework based on knowledge integration framework and technology acceptance model 2.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Graduate education in medical imaging is undergoing a paradigm shift from discipline-specific knowledge transmission toward the cultivation of multidisciplinary integration competencies. With the increasing convergence of imaging science, clinical medicine, engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, traditional training models that rely on fragmented, discipline-based curricula are insufficient to prepare graduate students for solving complex interdisciplinary problems. Although emerging educational technologies and learning platforms have been developed to promote interdisciplinary training, their effectiveness depends not only on the design of cognitive learning pathways but also on learners' acceptance and sustained engagement with these technologies; however, current educational frameworks rarely integrate cognitive mechanisms and technology acceptance factors within a unified model. Therefore, this study proposes a platform-driven, dual-theory integrated teaching framework to support multidisciplinary competency development in medical imaging graduate education from both cognitive and technological perspectives. METHODS: This study constructed a theoretical framework by integrating the knowledge integration framework (KIF) and technology acceptance model 2 (TAM2). The four cognitive processes of KIF-elicitation, addition, differentiation, and organization-were mapped onto four corresponding platform functions: activation of prior knowledge, exposure to industrial and clinical perspectives, authenticity-based knowledge verification, and multidisciplinary integrated output. Based on TAM2, design strategies for targeting perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were incorporated to explain the mechanisms underlying learners' acceptance, engagement, and utilization of the platform. By integrating KIF and TAM2, the framework established a dynamic learning pathway characterized by "knowledge activation-knowledge externalization-multidisciplinary integration-knowledge internalization". RESULTS: The proposed KIF-TAM2 framework demonstrated conceptual feasibility through theoretical modeling. However, its effectiveness in improving multidisciplinary learning outcomes requires further validation through empirical educational studies. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a theory-driven framework for designing multidisciplinary platform-based medical imaging education and offers a foundation for future empirical investigations into technology-enhanced graduate training.

articles.title: Native T1 mapping radiomics for assessing FIB-4-associated fibrosis risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) is widely used for noninvasive fibrosis risk stratification in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but it does not directly characterize spatial heterogeneity within the hepatic parenchyma. This study aimed to investigate whether native T1 mapping radiomics features are associated with continuous FIB-4 values in patients with MASLD, after accounting for hepatic steatosis and iron deposition with the goal of enabling early identification of liver fibrosis. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 124 patients with MASLD who underwent multiparametric liver magnetic resonance imaging, including proton density fat fraction (PDFF), iron (R2*), and native T1 mapping. To prevent data leakage, a 5-fold cross-validation framework was employed for radiomics analysis; variance thresholding, univariate Spearman correlation, and elastic net regression with nested cross-validation were performed sequentially within each training fold for feature selection and Z-score standardization. FIB-4 was treated as a continuous biochemical index, and two hierarchical regression models were refitted on the full dataset to evaluate the incremental value of the selected native T1 radiomics features beyond baseline liver fat (PDFF) and iron (R2*) content (Model 1: baseline; Model 2: baseline + radiomics features). In addition, we conducted an age-adjusted sensitivity analysis by including age as an additional covariate in both models to examine whether the contribution of radiomics features persists after accounting for age-related imaging variability. RESULTS: Twelve robust radiomics features were retained through the cross-validation selection pipeline. Model 1 showed limited explanatory ability for FIB-4 values (R2=0.028, adjusted R2=0.012, P=0.179). After incorporating the selected native T1 radiomics features, Model 2 demonstrated a significantly improved model fit (R2=0.455, adjusted R2=0.376; ΔR2=0.427; F-change =6.004, P<0.001). Root mean square error decreased from 0.167 to 0.133, and mean absolute error decreased from 0.132 to 0.106. In the age-adjusted sensitivity analysis, after controlling for age, PDFF, and R2*, the inclusion of radiomics features still significantly increased the explained variance, raising R2 from 0.428 to 0.631 (ΔR2=0.203, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Using FIB-4 as a clinical reference, and after excluding the effects of PDFF and R2*, a significant within-sample correlation was observed between the radiomics features generated by native T1 mapping and FIB-4 values, indicating its potential clinical utility in the noninvasive assessment of fibrosis-related biochemical risk trends in patients with MASLD.

articles.title: Glutamate-glutathione-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer 3-T magnetic resonance imaging for identifying malignant uterine tumors.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uterine tumors are a prevalent gynecological condition among women worldwide, and distinguishing malignant from benign uterine tumors is crucial for clinical decision-making. This study aimed to investigate the utility of Glutamate-glutathione-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer (Glu-GSHw-CEST) imaging for differentiating malignant from benign uterine tumors. METHODS: In this prospective study, participants were enrolled between April 2023 and February 2025. Ultimately, 57 patients, including 33 with benign tumors (33 uterine leiomyomas) and 24 with malignant tumors (15 cervical cancers and 9 endometrial cancers), were evaluated.T1-weighted imaging, T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and Glu-GSHw-CEST magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were performed with a 3-T clinical MRI scanner. Following B1 amplitude optimization at 3-T, a four-pool Lorentzian fitting model was used to extract the Glu-GSHw-CEST value from participants at 3 parts per million. The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) was calculated, and diagnostic efficacies were assessed via receiver operating characteristic curves analysis. The significance threshold was set at P<0.05. RESULTS: Malignant uterine tumors had a significantly higher Glu-GSHw-CEST effect than did benign tumors [7.942% (7.247%, 9.232%) vs. 6.773% (5.013%, 7.795%); U=234; P<0.001]. In distinguishing between malignant and benign uterine tumors, Glu-GSHw-CEST imaging [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) =0.750; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.631-0.869] and DWI (AUC =0.754; 95% CI: 0.619-0.890) showed comparable performance (P=0.966). Combining both methods further improved performance (AUC =0.868; 95%CI: 0.777-0.958) compared with Glu-GSHw-CEST (P=0.027) and DWI (P=0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Glu-GSHw-CEST is a promising noninvasive molecular imaging technique for differentiating malignant from benign uterine tumors at 3 T. Combining it with DWI can further enhance diagnostic performance.

articles.title: A DualDrop-Gated Transformer model for predicting bone metastasis in Asian patients with non-small cell lung cancer: a real-world study with external validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bone metastasis is a common and clinically important complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and is associated with poor survival. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) provides comprehensive skeletal assessment, its cost and radiation exposure may limit routine use. Therefore, an accessible approach based on routinely available clinical and chest CT-related information may help identify patients at higher risk who could benefit from further skeletal imaging. This study aimed to develop an effective predictive model for bone metastasis in patients with NSCLC. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed data from 17,646 Asian NSCLC patients in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2000-2021) as a training set and used an independent external cohort of 308 NSCLC patients from Shanghai Chest Hospital (2022-2023) for validation. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression (LR) analyses and Collinearity analysis were performed for variable selection. A novel DualDrop-Gated Transformer (DGT) model was developed and compared with LR, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), LightGBM, TabTransformer, and FTTransformer. Performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC), calibration, and decision curves. RESULTS: Age, sex, T stage, N stage, histological subtype, and lung metastasis status were identified as significant predicting variables. The DGT model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.947 in the training set, 0.936 in the internal test set, and 0.879 in the external validation cohort with balanced sensitivity (0.856) and specificity (0.934), significantly outperforming other models (P<0.01). Ablation experiments demonstrated the significant contributions of gating mechanisms and dropout to model performance. A nomogram based on the DGT model was constructed, with reasonable calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) revealed good clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: A novel DGT prediction model for bone metastasis in patients with NSCLC based on a highly generalizable and interpretable deep learning framework was developed and validated using 6 predictors, which may have potential application value in early screening, decision-making, and individualized management for lung cancer patients.

articles.title: The clinical efficacy of magnetic resonance neurography-assisted percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an imaging modality routinely used for the diagnosis of lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Conversely, magnetic resonance neurography (MRN), a novel magnetic resonance (MR)-based technique, has not yet been widely applied in the clinical management of LDH. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of combining MRN with MRI in guiding percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy (PTED) and to explore the potential clinical value of MRN. METHODS: Patients with LDH who met the inclusion criteria and were admitted to the Department of Orthopedics, Bengbu Third People's Hospital between April 2021 and April 2025 were retrospectively enrolled in the study. A total of 80 patients were included in the study (40 per group) and allocated to a control group (MRI only) and an observation group (MRI combined with MRN) based on whether a preoperative MRN examination was performed. Operative duration, the number of X-ray fluoroscopy sessions, the number of puncture attempts, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative hospital stay were compared between the groups. Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Japanese Orthopedic Association (JOA) scores were assessed at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups. Correlations between MRN parameters of the lumbosacral nerve on the affected and unaffected sides and preoperative JOA scores were further analyzed in the observation group. RESULTS: We compared the characteristics of the two groups of patients, baseline characteristics, including sex and age, were comparable between the two groups (P>0.05). In the observation group, the morphology and course of the nerve roots were visualized more clearly, providing valuable information for preoperative surgical planning. The observation group exhibited superior outcomes in terms of operative duration, the number of X-ray fluoroscopy sessions, the number of puncture attempts, and intraoperative blood loss compared with the control group (P<0.01); however, no significant difference in postoperative hospital stay was observed (P>0.05). Lower VAS scores were observed in the observation group at the 12-month postoperative follow-up, while higher JOA scores were observed at the 3-, 6-, and 12-month postoperative follow-ups (P<0.001). Significant differences in nerve root diameter, dorsal root ganglion length, and signal intensity were detected between the affected and unaffected sides in the observation group (P<0.05). Further, the difference in signal intensity was significantly correlated with the preoperative JOA score (r=0.721, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative MRN examination may facilitate preoperative assessment and surgical planning compared with conventional imaging modalities. The inter-side differences in MRN signal intensity parameters between the affected and unaffected sides, together with their observed correlations with JOA scores, provide preliminary evidence of the potential prognostic value of MRN.

articles.title: Risk factors for growth of small solid pulmonary nodules: a single-center retrospective case-control study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current clinical guidelines recommend conservative surveillance for 3-6 mm small solid pulmonary nodules (PNs), which may overlook a high-growth-risk subgroup. This study aimed to investigate independent risk factors for volume growth of small solid PNs and identify high-growth-risk subgroups. METHODS: This single-center retrospective case-control study enrolled patients with solid PNs (3 to <6 mm) who underwent chest computed tomography (CT) between January 2010 and December 2025. The growth group included nodules with volume increase >25% during follow-up; the stable group included nodules with volume change ≤25% over ≥5 years. Clinical characteristics and CT features were compared. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for growth. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the discriminatory ability of the multivariate regression model. RESULTS: A total of 175 patients were included, with 83 in the growth group and 92 in the stable group. Multivariate logistic regression identified coexistent emphysema [odds ratio (OR) =5.45, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.37-21.68, P=0.02], irregular shape (OR =3.05, 95% CI: 1.26-7.40, P=0.01), and pleural retraction (OR =4.99, 95% CI: 1.20-20.82, P=0.03) as independent risk factors for nodule growth. ROC curve analysis showed that the multivariate model achieved acceptable discriminatory performance with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.73-0.87). Among growth group cases, the median volume doubling time (VDT) was 364 days [interquartile range (IQR): 172-1,002 days]. Among the 28 nodules that underwent resection or biopsy, 75.0% (21/28) were malignant, whereas the remaining 25.0% (7/28) were benign. CONCLUSIONS: Emphysema, irregular shape, and pleural retraction are independent risk factors for growth in small solid PNs. Shortened CT surveillance intervals may be considered for patients with these high-risk signs. Given the single-center retrospective design without external validation, prospective multicenter verification is required for validation of this strategy.

articles.title: Photon-counting detector CT-derived extracellular volume fraction as a complementary biomarker for liver cirrhosis assessment: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) provides quantitative spectral and material decomposition information that may facilitate the noninvasive assessment of liver cirrhosis; however, the relative performance of PCD-CT-derived quantitative biomarkers for cirrhosis detection and severity stratification remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate PCD-CT-derived extracellular volume (ECV) fraction and other quantitative parameters, including liver fat fraction, portal venous phase iodine concentration (IC-PVP), delayed phase iodine concentration (IC-DP), normalized iodine concentration (nIC), and spectral slope, for cirrhosis assessment and functional severity stratification. METHODS: This single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 69 patients with cirrhosis and 43 control participants who underwent clinically indicated multiphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal PCD-CT between August and December 2025. Cirrhosis was confirmed histopathologically when available; otherwise, it was diagnosed using a composite clinical reference standard. Two radiologists independently measured ECV, fat fraction, iodine-based parameters, and spectral slope. Severity was assessed using Child-Pugh class, albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade, and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease sodium (MELD-Na) category. Logistic/ordered logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed, with bootstrap resampling used to assess the internal robustness of the main ROC estimates. RESULTS: Interobserver agreement was excellent [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), 0.94-0.98]. ECV was the only independent marker of cirrhosis [odds ratio (OR): 1.41; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.16-1.72; P<0.001]. It was also independently associated with increasing functional severity across Child-Pugh (adjusted OR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.23-1.69; P<0.001), ALBI (adjusted OR: 1.33; 95% CI: 1.12-1.58; P<0.001), and MELD-Na (adjusted OR: 1.38; 95% CI: 1.11-1.72; P=0.004). The area under the curve (AUC) for cirrhosis detection was 0.85, and for severity stratification ranged from 0.85 to 0.88; bootstrap resampling supported the internal robustness of the main ROC estimates. CONCLUSIONS: PCD-CT-derived ECV was independently associated with cirrhosis and functional severity categories defined by Child-Pugh, ALBI, and MELD-Na. It may serve as a complementary quantitative biomarker during clinically indicated contrast-enhanced PCD-CT.

articles.title: Radiomics-augmented lesion characterization on prostate multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging: first-order features and ratio metrics may improve diagnostic performance in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is increasingly recognized as an important diagnostic modality in the evaluation of prostate cancer. This analysis sought to investigate whether simple, ratio-normalized quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers obtained from routine mpMRI of the prostate provide incremental diagnostic value beyond the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System version 2.1 (PI-RADS v2.1) for the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 129 men underwent pre-biopsy 3-Tesla mpMRI followed by MRI/ultrasound fusion-guided biopsy. Quantitative first-order imaging features representing the three principal imaging domains underlying PI-RADS were derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging and normalized to intra-patient reference tissue. The analyses were performed on a lesion-specific basis and stratified by anatomical zone. Zone-specific logistic regression models were constructed to assess the incremental diagnostic value of quantitative biomarkers beyond PI-RADS v2.1. RESULTS: In the peripheral zone (PZ; 99 lesions), PI-RADS alone exhibited moderate discrimination for csPCa [area under the curve (AUC) =0.723]. An integrative model combining PI-RADS with prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) and quantitative MRI-derived ratios from DWI, T2WI, and DCE significantly improved discrimination [AUC =0.901, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.839-0.964]. After bootstrap-based optimism correction, the AUC decreased to 0.879. In the transition zone (TZ; 30 lesions), univariable analyses revealed no consistent differences in quantitative parameters between clinically significant and non-clinically significant lesions. PI-RADS alone yielded an AUC of 0.670, while ratio-based quantitative parameters did not provide meaningful incremental diagnostic value beyond PI-RADS v2.1. CONCLUSIONS: Simple, ratio-normalized quantitative MRI parameters integrated with PI-RADS and PSAD showed potential incremental value for detecting csPCa in the PZ. Conversely, these parameters demonstrated no statistically significant incremental diagnostic value beyond PI-RADS in the TZ in this limited cohort. These findings support a zone-aware, pragmatic approach to the quantitative augmentation of PI-RADS using routinely available MRI metrics.

articles.title: Echocardiographic epicardial adipose tissue thickness and coronary artery disease: a population-specific analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), but whether this relationship is linear and consistent across different demographic and metabolic subgroups remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to characterize the dose-response pattern of this association and to examine its variation across key demographic and metabolic subgroups. METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we enrolled 1,021 consecutive symptomatic patients who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) and echocardiography. EAT thickness was measured at end-systole using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the association between EAT thickness and CAD, and a trend analysis was performed by categorizing EAT thickness into quartiles. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to further characterize the dose-response relationship and test the linearity assumption. Interaction analyses were conducted to identify potential effect modifiers, and stratified analyses were additionally performed according to sex, age, hypertension, smoking status, HbA1c level, and HDL-C level. RESULTS: Among the 1,021 patients, 646 were diagnosed with CAD and had higher EAT thickness than those without CAD. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-mm increase in EAT thickness was associated with a 16% higher odds of CAD [odds ratio (OR): 1.16; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-1.26]. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile showed a markedly increased odds of CAD (OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.41-3.25), with a significant linear trend (P for trend =0.0024). RCS analysis further supported a linear dose-response relationship, showing no significant deviation from linearity (P for nonlinearity =0.544). Interaction analysis revealed a significant interaction between EAT thickness and BMI (P for interaction=0.017). In subgroup analyses, the association was stronger in individuals with a BMI <24 kg/m2, whereas no significant association was observed in those with a BMI ≥24 kg/m2. Descriptive findings also suggested that the association was stronger among males, older adults (≥55 years), individuals with hypertension, non-smokers, and those with HDL-C ≥1.04 mmol/L. CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic EAT thickness demonstrated a significant positive linear association with CAD, which was significantly modified by BMI, with a notably stronger effect observed in individuals with BMI <24 kg/m2. Routine echocardiographic assessment of EAT thickness may help identify individuals at higher CAD risk, particularly among those with a normal BMI.

articles.title: Ultrasonic texture features for assessing abnormal interventricular septum motion following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery alters cardiomyocyte geometry and architecture, leading to changes in the acoustic properties of the myocardium. This study investigated ultrasomics-a novel cardiac ultrasound-based radiomics technique that extracts high-throughput pixel-level information from images-to identify ultrasonic texture and morphological changes associated with abnormal motion of the interventricular septum (IVS) following cardiac surgery. METHODS: A total of 650 patients from two centers were included in the study. The 460 patients from Center A were randomly allocated to the training (n=322) and internal validation (n=138) sets at a 7:3 ratio, while the 190 patients from Center B constituted the independent external validation set. All patients underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at two time points: 10 minutes after anesthesia induction (preoperative) and 10 minutes after chest closure (postoperative). Standard left ventricular long-axis and four-chamber views were acquired to visualize the IVS. The workflow consisted of IVS segmentation, radiomics feature extraction, and feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Three machine learning methods were compared: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. RESULTS: Twenty-six significant radiomics features, including shape, first-order, and texture features, were identified. The incidence of postoperative abnormal IVS motion was 50.93%, 46.38%, and 40.00% in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (P>0.05). The SVM model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.943 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.925-0.961] in the training set, 0.948 (95% CI: 0.921-0.974) in the internal validation set, and 0.803 (95% CI: 0.772-0.834) in the external validation set. Postoperative analysis revealed significant changes in the core IVS radiomics features. Specifically, increased gray-scale heterogeneity and decreased texture correlation in the IVS were observed in patients with abnormal septal motion after cardiac surgery (all relevant P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the potential of cardiac ultrasomics to differentiate between normal and abnormal IVS motion in patients after cardiac surgery. A highly interpretable SVM ultrasomics model was developed based on texture and morphological features, providing quantitative characterization of microstructural changes in the IVS associated with abnormal motion following cardiac surgery and potentially supporting more precise perioperative clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Predicting immunotherapy response in patients with non-small cell lung cancer: superior performance of a positron emission tomography radiomics-based stacking ensemble model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The efficacy of immunotherapy among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) varies, and thus reliable predictive biomarkers of response are needed. This study aimed to develop and validate a stacking ensemble learning model based on pretreatment positron emission tomography (PET) radiomics to predict response to immunotherapy in patients with NSCLC. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 45 patients with NSCLC treated with immunotherapy were enrolled. Pretreatment Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine-format PET images were preprocessed and normalized. Tumor volumes were segmented using three methods: manual delineation, fixed standardized uptake value (SUV) thresholding with a standardized uptake value of 2.5 (SUV2.5), and adaptive thresholding (40% of the maximum SUV). Radiomics features were extracted, followed by a multistep feature selection process involving mutual information, Spearman correlation, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Predictive models constructed included a stacking ensemble model [with k-nearest neighbors (KNN), logistic regression (LR), and random forest (RF) as base learners], a clinical feature-based model, and a deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated on an independent test set according to the area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. RESULTS: On the test set, the stacking ensemble model achieved the highest predictive performance using features from the SUV2.5 segmentation dataset, with an AUC of 0.933 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.846-0.994]. This significantly outperformed the best single model (LR; AUC=0.896) and a deep learning model (AUC =0.925). The clinical feature-based model showed moderate predictive capability, with extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) yielding the highest AUC of 0.877 (95% CI: 0.644-1.000). CONCLUSIONS: The proposed PET radiomics stacking ensemble model, which leverages features from multiple segmentation strategies, demonstrated superior predictive performance for immunotherapy response in NSCLC compared to single models and other benchmarks. This approach offers an effective strategy for enhancing robustness in small-sample radiomics studies and holds promise as a noninvasive decision-support tool that can aid in personalized immunotherapy stratification.
